docs.title: A validated step retains the metric radius
docs.text:
The shared validated_metric_taylor_step now propagates the exact real set

\[ \mathcal E(c,r)=\{c+e:e^{\mathsf T}We\le r^2\}, \]

with a rational center c, rational positive-definite W and nonnegative radius r. Its enclosing coordinate box uses outward bounds on sqrt((W^(-1))_ii)r. That box is used for strict Picard inclusion and whole-time derivative and domain bounds; it does not replace the retained metric ball. In particular, the next step does not reconvert that enclosing box into a new metric radius.

Let h>0 be the step duration in the declared execution clock. Strict Picard inclusion must enclose the exact center flow and every flow starting in E(c,r). The model-specific growth inequality must hold throughout the resulting convex tube, including the segments between those flows. If its logarithmic bound is gamma, their separation at the endpoint obeys

\[ \|\Phi_h(c+e)-\Phi_h(c)\|_W\le e^{\gamma h}r. \]

Compute an interval Taylor polynomial from the exact center and its full order-p+1 remainder over the Picard tube. Let C_i be the resulting enclosure of the exact center endpoint, let c_i^+ be its exact rational midpoint and let a_i bound the distance from that midpoint to both materialized endpoints. Thus a_i includes Taylor truncation, interval arithmetic and any outward materialization of a nondyadic initial center. The local endpoint error satisfies

\[ \|\Phi_h(c)-c^+\|_W^2 \le\sum_{i,j}|W_{ij}|a_i a_j\le\ell^2 \]

when ell is chosen as an outward upper bound on the displayed square root. The triangle inequality therefore proves the retained-ball update

\[ \boxed{\Phi_h\bigl(\mathcal E(c,r)\bigr) \subseteq\mathcal E\left(c^+,\,e^{\gamma h}r+\ell\right).} \]

The local remainder is an endpoint error, so it is added after propagation of the initial radius. Every scalar exponential, square root and final radius is rounded outward. The current exact exponential evaluation admits abs(gamma*h)<=1; this is a numerical work limit, not a restriction of the mathematical inclusion. The generic kernel checks positive definiteness, Picard inclusion and the arithmetic. The caller remains responsible for the supplied logarithmic-norm theorem on the whole tube.

The retained endpoint ball can contain unreachable states or extend beyond the previous Picard tube. The next step therefore checks its whole initial projection again. Intersecting an observation box with an earlier tube would not justify shrinking this independent ball. Failed domain or remainder admission leaves only the already validated prefix available.

docs.title: Sine execution with retained full-state uncertainty
docs.text:
forecast_sine_saddle_metric re-admits the complete unit-capacity C5/private-leaf law, reconstructs the metric and advances the actual captured source with the shared sine field. It retains all twenty coordinates in source-node order: first every form, then every primitive phase. The common origins remain present, and no exact signed-family assumption is imposed on the uncertainty.

The API declares elapsed original structural time t. In its fixed saddle-domain mode, tau=t/pi gives the outward original-clock growth bound

\[ \gamma_t=\frac{1/3+28\rho}{\pi_{\rm lower}}. \]

Both forward and reverse field directions use the corresponding proved metric inequality. In that mode, every whole-time phase interval is compared with an outward enclosure of its exact saddle lift 2*pi*turn_i; neither a rounded value of pi nor an implicit phase wrap substitutes for this real-lift domain check. The positive domain margins apply to the nominal and perturbed flows together.

An independent initial coordinate cube is enclosed in the metric ball once. Successive steps carry only the exact recentered state and retained radius in the same metric. Coordinate endpoint intervals are observations of that ball, not the uncertainty representation consumed by the next step. Declared step, order, domain policy and work budget remain fixed: a failure does not authorize a larger domain or an undeclared retry.

docs.title: Certifying growth on a full Picard tube beyond the saddle neighborhood
docs.text:
The metric W itself is constant and positive definite on the entire twenty-coordinate state space. Only the previously supplied bound 1/3+28rho depends on remaining near the saddle. A direct Jacobian inequality on each complete Picard tube can replace that local bound without changing the metric, law or uncertainty representation.

Let J(z) be the Jacobian of the declared execution field on such a tube. Enclose every entry of the symmetric matrix

\[ S(z)=J(z)^{\mathsf T}W+WJ(z) \]

by symmetric rational intervals. Write their exact midpoint matrix as M and their symmetric nonnegative radius matrix as R. For every vector v,

\[ \begin{aligned} v^{\mathsf T}[S(z)-M]v &\le\sum_{i,j}R_{ij}|v_i v_j|\\ &\le\sum_i\left(\sum_jR_{ij}\right)v_i^2. \end{aligned} \]

Consequently the single exact matrix inequality

\[ \boxed{2\gamma W-M- \operatorname{diag}(R\mathbf1)\succeq0} \]

proves S(z)<=2gamma W at every point of the whole tube. It is a nonlinear flow bound because all possible Jacobians on that tube are enclosed, rather than just the Jacobian at its midpoint. Interval correlations discarded in forming the majorant can weaken the estimate, but cannot strengthen it without proof.

The shared step can select this route with growth_rate=None, a declared growth_rate_bounds bracket and a fixed growth_bisections count. The sine adapter's default bracket is (0,1) with eight exact positive-semidefiniteness bisections. The upper endpoint must first pass the matrix test; failure leaves the step unavailable, without expanding the bracket or changing the time step. Each selected rate and its matrix premises belong to the retained step evidence. This deterministic numerical policy is fixed before evaluating the reserved response; it does not fit or alter the nodal law.

For this sine model, W is block diagonal in form and phase, while J and hence S have only off-diagonal form/phase blocks. Conjugation by diag(I,-I) leaves W and the diagonal radius inflation unchanged and changes M to -M. Thus a successful matrix test also supplies the corresponding reverse-field inequality. This shortcut uses the admitted block structure; it is not a property of an arbitrary supplied Jacobian.

The sine adapter selects the tube-derived mode with phase_radius=None. It rebuilds the same full-state metric, then admits arbitrary primitive phase lifts under the globally smooth, fixed-support conservative sine law. Every actual tube still needs strict Picard inclusion and the matrix certificate. The saddle's primitive-phase radius is no longer a consumed growth premise. Since the shared automatic differentiation now acts on the original-time field, its J, S and certified gamma already contain the clock factor 1/pi; dividing the selected rate by pi again would be incorrect. The earlier fixed-domain mode keeps its separate clock conversion.

Across successful steps, the propagated part of the uncertainty is bounded by exp(sum_k gamma_k h_k) in the same metric, with each local endpoint error added by the retained-radius recurrence. There is no need to switch metrics or turn a coordinate observation box into an independent source when the trajectory leaves the small saddle neighborhood.

docs.title: Retained finite connection and its preparation boundary
docs.text:
A forward endpoint is wholly at zero winding only if every receiver edge has a certified unique principal branch and the branch sum gives W=0. On a backward leg from the same admitted preparation, acute retention requires a contiguous collection of whole-time tubes with all receiver gaps strictly in (-pi/2,pi/2), fixed winding +1 or -1, and total original-time length at least an outward upper bound on pi. A sampled event midpoint cannot establish the required scaled duration T=1. Time reversal relates those two legs along the same complete flow, including each admitted perturbed preparation.

The frozen declaration uses the rational preparation with epsilon=2^-32, independent errors 2^-100 in all twenty coordinates, both time directions, original-time horizon 256, unit steps, Taylor order 16, and the declared (0,1) growth bracket with eight bisections. Its first-endpoint/first-window rule was fixed before evaluation. The retained evidence bundle and manifest preserve the source, protocol, full response and verdict.

docs.title: An inverse-inclusion test separates an image from a preparation
docs.text:
The same retained step evidence supplies a sufficient inverse-inclusion test without a new trajectory. Write g_k for each outward metric growth factor and ell_k for its local endpoint error. Starting with P_0=1 and eta_0=0, propagate

\[ P_{k+1}=g_kP_k,\qquad \eta_{k+1}=g_k\eta_k+\ell_k. \]

Rounding these nonnegative products and sums upward retains valid upper bounds. Thus eta_F bounds the exact nominal endpoint's distance from the retained rational endpoint center c_F. The two-sided metric inequality also gives ||Phi_A(z)-Phi_A(c)||_W >= ||z-c||_W/P_F for admitted trajectories. On the boundary of the initial metric ball of radius r, the image is therefore at distance at least r/P_F from Phi_A(c).

The complete sine field is globally Lipschitz on the full real lift, so its finite-time flow is a global diffeomorphism. Its image boundary is the image of the initial boundary. A segment leaving that image from Phi_A(c) must meet this boundary; the distance bound forbids such a crossing inside the radius-r/P_F ball. Closure includes its boundary. The triangle inequality then proves

\[ \boxed{\mathcal E(c_F,q)\subseteq\Phi_A(\mathcal E(c,r)), \qquad q=\frac r{P_F}-\eta_F>0.} \]

This argument uses the already admitted forward trajectories and global invertibility, rather than assuming a candidate inverse trajectory stays inside an unverified domain. The reversing symmetry is an isometry of the block-diagonal metric. A positive q would therefore supply an explicit reflected source ball, and a coordinate cube of radius at most q/sqrt(sum_ij|W_ij|) inside it.

The solver propagates an enclosing initial metric ball, which is larger than the originally declared coordinate cube. To require preimages inside that cube of radius delta, use instead its admitted metric ball of radius r_in=delta/max_i sqrt((W^(-1))_ii), with an outward denominator. These are different preparation claims even though the same tubes can bound both.

The exact postprocessing record binds the retained response digest and recurrence, without a new forecast. Postprocessing the retained data through the first zero-winding endpoint gives outward bounds approximately P_F=7.60523305384e10 and eta_F=7.36366081855e-13. Both the enclosing-ball and inscribed-ball expressions for q are negative. Thus this sufficient test supplies no independent zero-winding preparation ball. It neither disproves the mapped connection nor establishes that an independent source ball is dynamically impossible. The finite connection, the incomplete forward horizon and the unavailable operational source width remain separate conclusions.

The local-agreement/global-storage discriminator keeps this frozen response intact while testing which constitutive premises its winding passage consumes. Agreement with the preparation, local saddle motion or acute geometry does not alone select a global pressure law.

docs.title: 52. A constitutive change preserves equilibria but blocks the same source's formation
docs.text: The declared comparison eta=1/100 gives an energetic obstruction, not merely an unavailable trajectory-error estimate. The same source that forms and retains acute winding under sine lies below the changed law's acquisition barrier. This result reuses the retained sine response; it requires no new trajectory, altered preparation or coefficient search.

docs.title: The complete changed law and fixed source
docs.text:
The cubic-storage completion keeps the C5/private-leaf support, held unit capacities and phase row:

\[ \begin{aligned} j_\eta(\delta)&=\sin\delta+\eta\sin^3\delta,\\ U_\eta(\delta)&=1-\cos\delta+ \eta\left(\frac23-\cos\delta+\frac{\cos^3\delta}{3}\right),\\ x'&=KS_\eta(\theta),\qquad \theta'=KLx, \qquad S_{\eta,i}=\sum_{j\sim i}j_\eta(\theta_j-\theta_i). \end{aligned} \]

Primes denote tau=t/pi; there are no inputs, events or discarded coordinates. For eta>=0, the changed nonnegative storage H_eta=x^T Lx/2+sum_e U_eta(delta_e) is conserved by its own reciprocal rows. The sine storage is not conserved by this changed field in general. The fixed scale eta=1/100 bounds the current change by one percent of normalized unit current. It is a declared robustness question, not a physical constant or a replacement engine default.

Use exactly the retained source family

\[ p_z=R\Phi^{\sin}_{237}(z),\qquad R(x,\theta)=(-x,\theta), \]

where z belongs to the frozen intermediate preparation. Flow times in this source definition are original structural time. Both laws start at this same exact p_z, whose zero winding is certified by the retained endpoint enclosure. Its sine reference path is

\[ y_z(s)=R\Phi^{\sin}_{237-s}(z),\qquad 0\le s\le471. \]

The whole sine interval [467,471] is acute with winding one, of scaled length 4/pi>1. Its retained tubes are forward steps 236,...,0 traversed in reverse and reflected, then backward steps 0,...,233 reflected. Preparing R Phi_eta,237(z) instead would change the source. An independent rectangular source ball or positive inverse-inclusion radius is unnecessary for this comparison of the same exact mapped states; the comparison does not supply either admission.

docs.title: The exact changed acquisition barrier
docs.text:
Keep the entire sector from Section 42:

\[ \Omega_\sigma=\{W=\sigma,\ |\delta_i|<2\pi/3\text{ for all five edges}\}, \qquad \sigma\in\{-1,1\}. \]

Every acute state of winding sigma belongs to this sector. For every eta>=0, the map s -> s+eta*s^3 is strictly increasing. Consequently j_eta(t)-j_eta(pi/3) is nonpositive on [-2pi/3,pi/3] and nonnegative on [pi/3,2pi/3]. Integrating gives the global tangent bound on this whole interval,

\[ U_\eta(t)\ge U_\eta(\pi/3)+j_\eta(\pi/3)(t-\pi/3). \]

On the positive-winding boundary with one gap 2pi/3, the other four sum to 4pi/3. Their linear terms therefore cancel, proving

\[ \boxed{B_\eta:=\min_{\partial\Omega_\sigma}\sum_iU_\eta(\delta_i) =U_\eta(2\pi/3)+4U_\eta(\pi/3) =\frac72+\frac{47}{24}\eta.} \]

Equality is attained by the five permutations of (2pi/3,pi/3,pi/3,pi/3,pi/3). A gap -2pi/3 forces the other four to be 2pi/3, and has the strictly larger cost 5U_eta(2pi/3). Evenness gives the negative-winding result. No nonnegative-gap restriction or small-eta approximation enters this minimum.

For each finite eta, the periodic current is bounded, so form grows at most linearly on bounded time intervals; the linear phase row then also remains finite. The smooth full flow therefore exists in both time directions. All other full-system storage is nonnegative. Thus H_eta<B_eta forbids sector-boundary crossing in either time direction. Equality also forbids a finite crossing: it forces constant form and zero contact storage, while all cycle currents at the minimizing geometry are equal. The entire state is then stationary, and uniqueness excludes reaching or leaving it at finite time from a different state. Therefore a source outside both sectors with H_eta<=B_eta cannot acquire acute winding +1 or -1 at any time. This does not prohibit nonacute winding outside these sectors or identify every possible future state.

docs.title: Applying the barrier to the retained source
docs.text:
Define the nonnegative added phase storage on all ten edges,

\[ A(\theta)=\sum_e\frac{(1-\cos\delta_e)^2(\cos\delta_e+2)}3. \]

Sine conservation and form reversal give the exact source identity

\[ H_\eta(p_z)=H_0(z)+\eta A(\theta(p_z)). \]

Here H_0(z) is bounded from the original preparation, and A is bounded from the complete retained endpoint at original time 237. Neither term uses the changed law's unknown response. The retained evidence contains the initial full-state enclosure and forward endpoint 236. The constitutive comparison record binds those retained premises without modifying the frozen response. Outward evaluation gives, conservatively rounded,

\[ 1.71785519306<A(\theta(p_z))<1.71785519309, \] \[ H_{1/100}(p_z)<3.51717855194 <B_{1/100}=\frac72+\frac{47}{2400}, \qquad B_{1/100}-H_{1/100}(p_z)>0.00240478139. \]

The full source enclosure has winding zero. Thus the declared cubic law cannot acquire either acute unit-winding identity from any member of this same source family, although sine certifies the retained finite window. This is an all-time acquisition obstruction under the changed complete law, not evidence that an already formed identity disappears, that no other preparation can form it, or that the sine result was incorrect.

The sharp budget comparison can also be written

\[ B_\eta-H_\eta(p_z)= \eta\left(\frac{47}{24}-A(\theta(p_z))\right) -\left(H_0(z)-\frac72\right). \]

It explains the sensitivity: the sine construction uses a very small excess above its own saddle barrier, while the changed law raises that barrier more than it raises this fixed source's storage. A positive budget margin above a law's barrier is necessary for crossing, not a sufficient formation theorem. This identity supplies no instruction to retune the source until a preferred outcome passes.

docs.title: The complete critical geometry and its inertia remain unchanged
docs.text:
The effect is not removal of the critical patterns. On this connected support, equilibrium requires constant form. Each private leaf has one neighbor and must have contact phase 0 or pi modulo 2pi. Cycle stationarity then requires one common oriented value of j_eta(delta). Its strict monotonicity as a function of sin(delta) makes this exactly the sine condition: all oriented cycle sines have the same value s. Thus the entire critical phase set is unchanged for every eta>=0.

At any such critical state the cycle Hessian weights are

\[ U_\eta''(\delta_i)=(1+3\eta s^2)\cos\delta_i, \]

while contact Hessian weights remain +1 or -1. Change phase coordinates to the receiver phases and the five leaf-minus-receiver contrasts. The phase quadratic splits into a positive scalar 1+3eta*s^2 times the original cycle quadratic plus the five unchanged signed contact squares. This is a congruence argument, so the full phase Hessian has the same inertia, including nullity. The full Hessian is not generally a common scalar multiple: the cycle and contact blocks scale differently. The form quadratic and mobility are unchanged, but individual dynamical rates and frequencies need not be.

This extends the prepared-geometry result to the entire critical set on the present unicyclic support. It explains why matching equilibrium geometries or their stability types cannot establish matching accessibility from one fixed preparation.

docs.title: The sufficient error-transport method has a separate role
docs.text:
A finite comparison can also write the original-time fields as F_eta=F_0+eta D, where only the form rows of D are nonzero and each has absolute value at most 1/pi. For the retained block metric,

\[ \|D\|_W\le\frac{\sqrt{\sum_{i,j}|(W_x)_{ij}|}}{\pi_{\rm lower}}\le M. \]

On a common convex tube with admitted original-time sine logarithmic rate gamma, the paired-state error starting at e_0 obeys

\[ e(s)\le e^{\gamma s}e_0+|\eta|M\varphi(\gamma,s),\qquad \varphi(\gamma,s)=\begin{cases}(e^{\gamma s}-1)/\gamma,&\gamma\ne0,\\ s,&\gamma=0.\end{cases} \]

Initially the paired error is zero because the source is identical. The retained Picard image initial_box+[0,h]*direction*F_0(tube) gives strict clearance of the reference path inside each tube, also after reflection and reverse traversal. Keeping every coordinate projection sqrt((W^-1)_ii)*max e(s) below that clearance closes the common-domain premise by first exit. On target tubes, subtract the sum of both endpoint phase-error bounds from every strict acute margin. The block symmetry from Section 51 supplies the needed direction change, and its retained rates already contain the original clock factor 1/pi.

Numerical enclosure error and intermediate preparation uncertainty enter those retained domains and margins; they are not extra constitutive forcing. A failed sufficient bound would only leave the comparison unavailable. Here the stronger conserved-budget obstruction already settles the fixed-scale question, so no 471-step defect-transport campaign, coefficient reduction or new trajectory is needed. Neither this negative comparison nor critical-geometry agreement selects a fundamental law or establishes physical identification.

It re-admits the frozen source, preparation, support and required endpoint evidence before rebuilding the changed storage and sector barrier. It neither installs the changed law nor executes a new forecast.

docs.text:
The complete global sine comparison; common exchange geometry, form balance, storage alternatives, first-moment restrictions and form-origin information premises.

Part of Native relational exchange admission. Section numbers are stable across the collection; hypotheses and model changes remain local to each result.

docs.title: 11.6 Global closure obstruction and a normalized-sine comparison
docs.text: The finite-time boundary audit requires distinguishing a limited-domain law from a globally defined one. The pressure owner already proves that principal-argument pressure has no continuous extension through either an antipodal branch or a zero neighbor resultant. With w*nu_i>0 the form row inherits that discontinuity. Changing only phase evolution, storage or locality cannot repair it while leaving that form row unchanged. The reflected boundary additionally has path-dependent phase-rate limits from positive resultants. A regular invertible chart change removes neither obstruction.

docs.title: The incompatibility is stronger than the local-completion theorem
docs.text:
Take P2 with r=x_0-x_1!=0, delta=theta_1-theta_0 in (-pi,pi), c=nu_0+nu_1>0 and arbitrary phase velocities F_0,F_1. The native form row and current storage give, before any locality assumption,

\[ E=r^2/2+\beta(1-\cos\delta),\qquad \dot E=c[-er^2+wr\delta/\pi]+\beta\sin\delta(F_1-F_0). \]

Preserving the prescribed exact loss forces

\[ F_0-F_1=\frac{wcr\delta}{\beta\pi\sin\delta}. \]

This relative rate diverges as delta->pi at fixed nonzero form contrast. It is unaffected by a common phase clock. Dropping capacity separability or allowing nonlocal phase rows therefore cannot supply a bounded completion with the same pressure, storage and loss.

Even weakening exact loss to total passivity is insufficient. If F were bounded near this antipodal state, its phase-work term would tend to zero, leaving lim Edot=c*(-e*r^2+w*r). For e>0 choose 0<r<w/e; for e=0 any r>0 suffices. The limit is positive, contradicting passivity. This argument concerns all-state work identities, not an assertion that these fixed-form paths are trajectories. Actual finite-time collisions have their separate proof. The bounded rho*Ng and fixed-form nonlinear phase corrections above retain their regular-domain results but cannot cure this global obstruction.

Retained requirement What it forces or leaves open Native principal-argument form pressure on the same circular full state No globally continuous extension; phase-only changes cannot resolve it That pressure, cosine storage and exact global loss Unbounded relative phase response near antipodal P2, without needing locality That pressure, cosine storage and only total passivity Still incompatible with bounded phase completion on all finite form states Restricted invariant preparations Remain legitimate limited-domain models; the sufficient storage theorem and protected basins apply Changed pressure, enlarged state, event or generalized solution convention Separate model obligations; none is supplied by assigning a numerical value at zero

docs.title: Reuse an existing phase reading with an explicit changed premise
docs.text:
The repository already distinguishes J_phi/pi from argument pressure. Write S_i=sum_j sin(theta_j-theta_i), q=Bx and D=diag(d_i) on fixed connected simple unit support. The following comparison law uses the same signed form, circular phase, held nonnegative capacity and clock:

\[ s_i=\frac{S_i}{\pi d_i},\qquad \boxed{\dot x=N(-eD^{-1}q+ws),\quad \dot\theta=\frac{w}{\beta\pi}ND^{-1}q.} \]

Its phase-to-form pressure is s=J_phi/pi and its response metric is H_s=pi*D. This replaces both native phase-pressure response and its matching exchange row. It is not the native law with a different domain setting, and not the separately supplied Kuramoto/U3 sine phase clock: here sine enters form pressure, while form contrast drives phase. Existing current telemetry does not select its use as a dynamical law.

On the native regular domain,

\[ s_i=\frac{|z_i|}{d_i}\operatorname{sinc}(\operatorname{Arg}z_i)\,g_i. \]

Thus the existing geometric relation directly relates the two responses. The comparison retains cancellation strength as well as direction, and has no division by a resultant or its argument. It remains defined when phases cancel. No new primitive variable, cutoff, fitted gain or boundary event is introduced. Choosing this pressure is nevertheless an additional premise.

docs.title: Complete balance, continuation and inherited geometry
docs.text:
With the unchanged storage E=E_D+beta*V_phi, grad V_phi=-S gives

\[ \dot E_D=-e q^TND^{-1}q+\frac w\pi q^TND^{-1}S,\qquad \beta\dot V_\phi=-\frac w\pi S^TND^{-1}q. \]

The exchange cancels exactly, leaving the same loss -e q^TND^{-1}q. On any fixed finite graph the complete vector field is globally Lipschitz on the form/phase lift: its form dependence is linear with constant coefficients, and sine has bounded derivative. Hence every finite initial state has a unique global solution, descending to circular phases. This mathematical theorem concerns the comparison, not the native executor.

For strictly positive held capacities, reciprocity supplies two identities:

\[ \frac{d}{dt}\sum_i\frac{d_i}{\nu_i}x_i=0,\qquad \frac{d}{dt}\sum_i\frac{d_i}{\nu_i}\theta_i=0. \]

The second uses a chosen continuous phase lift; it is not in general a single-valued scalar observation on the phase torus. At zero capacity these weighted expressions are unavailable, although the smooth law and work balance remain valid. The native law generally conserves neither mean.

With all capacities positive, equilibria are exactly q=0,S=0. All native regular equilibria therefore survive, but the complete set grows: zero and negative-real resultants with S=0 are now allowed. The seven-equilibrium classification must not be transferred as exhaustive. At each equilibrium the existing full-network stiffness proof applies with H=pi*D: positive quotient cosine Hessian gives local exponential recovery for e,w,beta>0, and negative stiffness gives growing real modes. Consensus has exactly the native linearization. Away from consensus, equal geometry and stability signs do not give equal rates, memory or basins.

For e>0 and positive capacities, storage and conserved weighted form mean give precompactness on form times the phase torus. On the largest invariant subset with zero loss, q=0 and BND^-1 S=0, so ND^-1 S=c*1. Reciprocity sum_i S_i=0 forces c=0. LaSalle therefore gives approach to the equilibrium set. This does not prove convergence to consensus, to one equilibrium, or to a physical entity.

docs.title: Conditional selection and remaining freedom
docs.text:
There is a more structural selection route than assuming a constant metric. Keep cosine storage, the same diffusion channel and exact loss on the full phase torus for every finite connected simple unit graph and every nonnegative capacity vector. Require zero-capacity phase freezing, own-capacity separability and a finite continuous phase law. The additional pressure premise is normalized pairwise superposition,

\[ g_i(\theta)=d_i^{-1}\sum_{j\sim i}f(\theta_j-\theta_i), \]

with one continuous, periodic, odd kernel f across supports. On a star with only the root active and arbitrary q_i!=0, exact loss gives beta*S_i*F_i=w*nu_i*q_i*g_i. Thus every finite family with sum_j sin(delta_j)=0 must also have sum_j f(delta_j)=0. All phases, including cancellations and antipodal leaves, are admitted by the proposed global completion; no regular-domain padding is required.

Reuse the balanced-star algebra with a different object being classified. The two gaps delta,-arcsin(sin(delta)) give f(delta)=f(arcsin(sin(delta))). Put h(s)=f(arcsin(s)). Three gaps with sines a,b,-(a+b) give h(a+b)=h(a)+h(b) whenever all arguments lie in [-1,1]. Continuity implies h(s)=k*s and therefore f(delta)=k*sin(delta). Matching the native consensus tangent fixes k=1/pi. Capacity isolation now forces F_i=w*nu_i*q_i/(beta*pi*d_i) whenever S_i!=0; own-capacity separability transfers this row to general capacities. Nonzero S_i states are dense by perturbing a neighbor phase, including near zero resultants, so continuity extends the row everywhere. Varying only the root phase would not justify that density at a zero neighbor resultant.

This derives the metric and phase independence instead of assuming them. It does not derive pairwise superposition, which the native collective Arg source does not obey. A separate sufficient selection premise is to require the phase row itself to be phase-independent while leaving the phase-only pressure initially unrestricted: the same isolated-capacity identity and consensus tangent then also force the displayed comparison.

Neither selection premise follows from smoothness, storage or circular symmetry. For example, the comparison family

\[ m_i(\theta)=\frac{1+\epsilon(S_i/d_i)^2}{\pi d_i},\quad g_i=m_iS_i,\quad F_i=(w/\beta)\nu_i m_i q_i,\qquad \epsilon\ge0 \]

retains smoothness, positive mobility, exact loss, the same equilibria and the same consensus Jacobian. It supplies a counterexample to unique selection, not another production setting. The frozen pairing comparison reuses its zero-loss members to separate a robust local grouping direction from different relative response rates. The family generally violates the common pairwise-superposition premise. The original storage classification assumed native pressure; changing that premise means cosine storage is retained here explicitly, not rederived by that old theorem.

docs.title: An exact discriminator before any trajectory
docs.text:
On a three-leaf star, take center phase zero, leaf phases (0,0,pi/2), uniform form and positive held capacities. All native resultants are regular. Put W=sum_i d_i/nu_i and let M be the degree/inverse-capacity weighted form mean. At this same initial state,

\[ \dot M_{\rm native} =\frac wW\left[\frac{3\arctan(1/2)}{\pi}-\frac12\right]<0,\qquad \dot M_{\rm sine}=0. \]

The sign follows from atan(1/2)<1/2<pi/6. Both initial phase rates are zero, and both laws dissipate zero storage initially; the mean response still distinguishes them. This is an exact prospective initial-rate comparison with identical preparation, coefficients and clock, not a fitted response or physical validation. The older same-mean/different-spread pressure test remains useful; no frozen acquisition is rerun.

There is also a purely spectral distinction at the same maintained C5 geometry. For a uniform acute cycle twist with c=cos(kappa)>0, common capacity nu and nonzero combinatorial Laplacian eigenvalue ell, write z=2*s/(nu*ell) for the scaled temporal exponent. The two characteristic polynomials are

\[ z^2+ez+\frac{w^2}{\beta\pi^2c}=0\quad\text{(native)},\qquad z^2+ez+\frac{w^2c}{\beta\pi^2}=0\quad\text{(comparison)}. \]

For winding-one C5, e=w=1/2,beta=1 and c=cos(2*pi/5)<1/3. The native discriminant 1/4-1/(pi^2*c) is negative, whereas the comparison discriminant 1/4-c/pi^2 is positive. Both recover locally, but one has damped oscillatory linear modes and the other distinct negative real modes. Local pulse character therefore depends on the constitutive response, even when the stable geometry and storage agree. This is a tangent theorem, not a computed nonlinear response or a transfer of earlier memory records.

bound_relational_sine_exchange is a detached static comparison with explicit law identity and exact represented-state trigonometric bounds. It reuses shared graph/scalar admission and report projection, while preserving native phase-domain rejection. Its computed interval work residuals are distinct from the analytic cancellation identity. It installs no dynamics, boundary extension or automatic model selector. Frozen transit, capture, memory and formation responses remain evidence of their original law.

docs.title: 11.7 Common exchange geometry, composition and a controlled common regime
docs.text:
The two complete laws above belong to one mathematical family. This is an identity between declared models, not a derivation of a uniquely selected microscopic law. Keep the same support, clock, held capacities, coefficients and storage. Write M=diag(m_i) with finite positive entries on its stated domain. Then

\[ \dot x=N(-eD^{-1}q+wMS),\qquad \dot\theta=(w/\beta)NMq \]

gives Edot=-e*q^T*N*D^-1*q for every such mobility. In fact grad_x E=q and grad_theta E=-beta*S, so the two exchange work terms cancel by symmetry of NM. No derivative of M enters this first storage derivative, even if M depends on the state. Existence, regularity, symmetries and higher derivatives still require their own hypotheses. Equal loss functions do not imply equal storage histories along different trajectories.

The native choice is m_i=1/H_i, while the normalized-sine comparison uses m_i=1/(pi*d_i). The common skew work structure therefore leaves precisely the constitutive mobility being investigated. It does not by itself give a Poisson bracket: the earlier Jacobi audit distinguishes that extra requirement from work cancellation.

docs.title: Geometric attenuation is not generally a change of clock
docs.text:
On the native regular domain put z_i=R_i*exp(i*alpha_i). The exact ratio is

\[ a_i=\frac{m_i^{\rm sine}}{m_i^{\rm native}} =\frac{R_i}{d_i}\operatorname{sinc}\alpha_i =\frac{H_i}{\pi d_i},\qquad 0<a_i\le1. \]

Here R_i<=d_i and 0<sinc(alpha_i)<=1. Equality requires all neighbors to have the center's phase modulo a turn. The sine law scales both nodal exchange terms by a_i and leaves form diffusion unchanged. Different nodes generally have different attenuations.

Even P2 with positive diffusion rules out a common clock interpretation. Set r=x_0-x_1, delta=theta_1-theta_0 in (-pi,pi) and c=nu_0+nu_1>0. In these two relative coordinates the native and sine velocity vectors are

\[ F_n=\left(c[-er+w\delta/\pi], -\frac{cw r\delta}{\beta\pi\sin\delta}\right),\qquad F_s=\left(c[-er+w\sin\delta/\pi], -\frac{cw r}{\beta\pi}\right). \]

Thus

\[ \det(F_n,F_s)=\frac{c^2ewr^2}{\beta\pi} \left(1-\frac{\delta}{\sin\delta}\right)\ne0 \]

when e>0,r!=0,0<|delta|<pi. A regular common clock change multiplies the whole vector field by one positive scalar, so it cannot identify these fields, even after removing common offsets. For e=0 on P2 only, F_s=sinc(delta)*F_n: there is a restricted orbit equivalence. It is not general on larger graphs; the preceding star's weighted-mean discriminator also applies at e=0 and forbids a positive common multiplier there.

docs.title: A controlled near-alignment regime
docs.text:
Suppose all wrapped incident gaps satisfy |delta_ij|<=epsilon<pi/2. Then C_i>=d_i*cos(epsilon) and |alpha_i|<=epsilon. Since H_i/pi=C_i*tan(alpha_i)/alpha_i>=C_i with the removable value at zero,

\[ \cos\epsilon\le a_i\le1,\qquad |g_i-s_i|\le\frac{(1-\cos\epsilon)\epsilon}{\pi}, \] \[ |\dot\theta_i^{\,n}-\dot\theta_i^{\,s}| \le\frac{w\nu_i|q_i|}{\beta\pi d_i}(\sec\epsilon-1),\qquad |\dot x_i^{\,n}-\dot x_i^{\,s}| \le\frac{w\nu_i}{\pi}(1-\cos\epsilon)\epsilon. \]

These are instantaneous bounds at a shared state, not trajectory enclosures. The phase discrepancy is O(epsilon^2*|q_i|); the complete discrepancy is cubic only when form contrasts are also O(epsilon). A future error estimate must additionally bound the field Lipschitz constant and preserve the neighborhood throughout the comparison horizon. The common small-signal regime is derived; the ratio does not supply an autonomous switching rule.

docs.title: Composition exposes an independent premise
docs.text:
At a fixed root state let P(A) be the phase source of a nonempty finite multiset of incident gaps A; equal entries mean different neighbors with the same phase, not parallel edges. Independent normalized composition would require, for every partition into disjoint incident groups,

\[ (|A|+|B|)P(A\sqcup B)=|A|P(A)+|B|P(B). \]

Induction over singleton groups makes this condition equivalent to P(A)=sum_{delta in A} f(delta)/|A| with f(delta)=P({delta}). It is exactly the added superposition premise used in the preceding classification, rather than a consequence of that classification.

Both candidates pass equal replication: duplicating every incident coordinate multiplies d,S,H,q by the same factor and preserves their complete nodal rates. That test is strictly weaker than independent composition. For example, take A=(0,0), B=(t) with 0<t<pi/2. Native source composition would require Arg(2+exp(i*t))=t/3. Instead

\[ \frac{d}{dt}\left[\operatorname{Arg}(2+e^{it})-\frac t3\right] =\frac{2(\cos t-1)}{3(5+4\cos t)}<0. \]

The merger defect is nonzero although all groups are regular. Sine sources obey the merger identity exactly. The smooth collective counterfamily in section 11.6 also preserves replication while generally violating merger. Neither nodal locality nor replication establishes independent composition.

The stationary mediator reduction answers the associated scale question constructively: even a primitive pairwise sine law induces collective visible interaction after eliminating one node. It shares the native conditional minimum and inherited storage, but transmits a different pressure. An emergent Arg coordinate is therefore not a derivation of native Arg pressure. Finite hidden capacity retains a tracking defect and memory; its controlled fast limit has explicit premises.

The composition controls exercise merger, replication, the local discrepancy bounds and clock non-equivalence using existing field owners. The detached mediation report integrates the justified reduction without selecting a new primitive law. Together these results identify a common exchange geometry and a common local regime, while leaving the deeper mobility-selection hypothesis open.

docs.title: 11.8 Closed form balance can select primitive pressure composition
docs.text:
The composition premise has an equivalent whole-graph interpretation within an explicit information class. This supplies another conditional selection route; neither conservation nor that information class follows from the nodal identity. Here a closed graph means that the entire fixed support is included, with no external source or event. Degree-one vertices are allowed.

Keep finite connected simple unit support with at least two nodes, held positive capacities, the support Laplacian B=D-A and q=Bx from section 1, and the form row

\[ \dot x=N(-eD^{-1}Bx+wg),\qquad e\ge0,\quad w>0. \]

Require one common phase-source family across supports, g_i=P_{d_i}(A_i), where A_i is the multiset of circular incident gaps theta_j-theta_i. The source consumes only these gaps and their count. It does not consume form, capacity, neighbor degrees, connections between neighbors, graph identity, or hidden state. Equal gaps can represent distinct neighbors. This is stronger than unspecified one-hop locality: replacing the root's environment by a star must preserve its source. No phase row or storage identity is needed for the next equivalence.

docs.title: Diffusion fixes the weight of a possible linear form invariant
docs.text:
For e>0, suppose a nonzero state-independent vector a, allowed to depend on the held graph and capacities, makes a^T*x invariant at every form and phase state. Varying form at fixed phase removes the phase-only source and gives

\[ a^TND^{-1}B=0,\qquad BD^{-1}Na=0. \]

Connectedness gives ker(B)=span{1}, hence a_i=c*d_i/nu_i for one nonzero constant c. Thus the only possible nontrivial linear form invariant has, up to scale, the weights

\[ \mathcal Q=\sum_i\frac{d_i}{\nu_i}x_i,\qquad W=\sum_i\frac{d_i}{\nu_i},\qquad M=\mathcal Q/W. \]

This identifies the weight if such an invariant is required; it does not establish its existence. For e=0 this uniqueness argument is unavailable. For the displayed weight and any e>=0, the exact accounting identity is

\[ \dot{\mathcal Q}=w\sum_i d_i g_i. \]

The positive-capacity premise matters: these inverse-capacity quantities are unavailable at a zero-capacity node.

docs.title: Whole-graph balance is equivalent to an odd pairwise source
docs.text:
In the gap-only source class, require sum_i d_i*g_i=0 for every phase state on every finite connected support. It suffices to require this on every star. Put f(delta)=P_1({delta}). On the single-edge graph the two root gaps are delta and -delta, so balance gives f(delta)+f(-delta)=0. On a star with root phase zero and arbitrary leaf phases delta_1,...,delta_d, the root has source P_d(A) and each leaf has source f(-delta_j). Therefore

\[ 0=dP_d(A)+\sum_{j=1}^d f(-\delta_j),\qquad \boxed{P_d(A)=\frac1d\sum_{j=1}^d f(\delta_j),\quad f(-\delta)=-f(\delta).} \]

Conversely, summing this formula over any reciprocal graph cancels the two orientations of each edge. Whole-graph balance is therefore equivalent to normalized pairwise superposition with one odd circular kernel, and to the preceding independent normalized-composition identity together with singleton oddness. No continuity or differentiability is used. Requiring the balance at one positive capacity assignment per star is enough because the source is capacity-independent and the capacities cancel from the accounting identity.

The support and information quantifiers cannot be discarded. Testing only regular graphs permits g_i=a_{d_i}*sum_j sin(delta_ij)/d_i with arbitrary degree-dependent gains. Consuming neighbor degrees instead permits

\[ g_i=\frac1{d_i}\sum_{j\sim i}(d_i+d_j)\sin\delta_{ij}, \]

which conserves the same weighted form on every graph by edge cancellation, but has no common singleton kernel across supports. It lies outside the stated gap-only information class. Ordinary locality, relabeling covariance or equal replication does not supply the missing restriction.

docs.title: Cosine exchange selects sine, with a separate phase-row premise
docs.text:
Combine this conservation premise with the global comparison domain and storage assumptions of section 11.6: continuous circular pressure on the full phase torus, the retained storage E_D+beta*V_phi, its exact loss -e*q^T*N*D^-1*q, and finite phase velocities that freeze at zero own capacity. The complete law must admit all nonnegative held capacity vectors; weighted form itself is used only on the positive-capacity part of that domain.

Activate only a star's root capacity and choose q_root!=0. All other phase rows freeze, so exact loss leaves

\[ \beta S_{\rm root}F_{\rm root} =w\nu_{\rm root}q_{\rm root}P_d(A). \]

Whenever sum_j sin(delta_j)=0, finiteness forces sum_j f(delta_j)=0. The balanced-star argument in section 11.6 then gives f(delta)=k*sin(delta); matching the native consensus tangent fixes k=1/pi. Thus conservation plus the stated global exchange premises selects the normalized-sine pressure without independently assuming pairwise superposition. This reuses the existing classification rather than deriving cosine storage or conservation from it.

Own-capacity separability is an additional requirement for selecting the complete phase row. With that premise and continuity of the phase law, capacity isolation at each node first forces the row where S_i!=0, transfers it to arbitrary capacity vectors, and extends it by continuity to S_i=0:

\[ g_i=\frac{S_i}{\pi d_i},\qquad F_i=\frac{w\nu_iq_i}{\beta\pi d_i}. \]

Without the extra phase-row premise, the pressure selection does not remove all globally work-null phase velocities. The required conservation law, cosine storage, prescribed loss, capacity behavior, full phase domain and consensus normalization remain independent constitutive assumptions.

docs.title: The combined premises also cover induced-neighborhood pressure
docs.text:
The sine-pressure conclusion survives a larger information class when both conservation and exact cosine exchange are imposed. Allow pressure to consume the phases and topology of the induced rooted ball G[{i} union N(i)], including edges between neighbors. Require one rule invariant under rooted isomorphism and common phase rotation across all supports, independent of form and capacity. External neighbor degrees, remote state and hidden support-specific coefficients remain excluded. This does not extend the conservation-alone equivalence to arbitrary local sources.

First isolate one active capacity in the global storage identity. For every node, S_i=0 forces g_i=0: choose q_i!=0, use finiteness of its phase row and freezing of all other phase rows. This implication holds at every capacity assignment because pressure is capacity-independent. On P2, whole-graph balance again makes the common singleton kernel f odd.

Adapt the induced-neighborhood completion. Retain an arbitrary root ball with all its internal edges and phases. For each root neighbor j and every retained incidence j-k, attach one private leaf to j with phase 2*theta_j-theta_k. No new leaf touches the root, so its entire source information is unchanged. Every retained neighbor now has S_j=0, and hence g_j=0, because each old sine contribution has its opposite at the reflected leaf. Unlike the native regular-domain completion, no aligned padding is needed: the full phase torus admits zero or negative resultants.

Assign strictly positive capacities throughout this completed graph before using whole-graph form balance. A reflected leaf at j-k contributes f(theta_k-theta_j). Leaves associated with the two incidences of an edge between root neighbors cancel by oddness. The remaining leaves correspond to root edges and contribute -sum_{j~i}f(theta_j-theta_i). Therefore

\[ d_i g_i=\sum_{j\sim i}f(\theta_j-\theta_i). \]

The original root inherits this identity by uniform rooted locality. The preceding balanced-star classification now selects normalized sine. No locality or capacity separability of the phase row was used to select this pressure; uniqueness of its complete phase row retains the earlier extra premise. The proof never evaluates inverse-capacity form weights at zero capacity. These completion graphs are mathematical comparison states, not support events. The locality controls check the retained root ball and reflected-leaf cancellation separately from the existing native-domain completion.

docs.title: Branching tests information that paths and cycles cannot determine
docs.text:
Even conservation, composition, smoothness, the consensus tangent and exact cosine-storage loss on every path and cycle do not select sine. For epsilon>0, take the common odd kernel

\[ f_\epsilon(\delta)=\frac{\sin\delta+\epsilon\sin^3\delta}{\pi}. \]

On graphs of maximum degree two, let s_j=sin(delta_j) at a root and use the finite positive mobility

\[ m_1=\frac{1+\epsilon s_1^2}{\pi},\qquad m_2=\frac{1+\epsilon(s_1^2-s_1s_2+s_2^2)}{2\pi}. \]

The identity s_1^3+s_2^3=(s_1+s_2)(s_1^2-s_1*s_2+s_2^2) gives P_d=m_d*S. Consequently F_i=(w/beta)*nu_i*m_i*q_i supplies a smooth full-state exchange completion with the prescribed exact loss, zero-capacity freezing and own-capacity separability on this restricted support class. Its tangent is the normalized-sine tangent, but its nonlinear pressure differs.

A degree-three star rejects that same kernel. Choose the acute leaf gaps (arcsin(1/4),arcsin(1/4),-pi/6). Their sine sum is zero while their sine cubes sum to -3/32, giving

\[ P_3=-\frac{\epsilon}{32\pi}\ne0. \]

With only the root capacity active and nonzero root form contrast, its phase work is zero and its source work is nonzero. No finite phase row with the stated freezing can supply the prescribed loss. The obstruction occurs strictly inside an acute phase chart, not only at a zero resultant or an antipodal boundary. Degree-three branching is therefore indispensable to this countercontrol; further path or cycle trajectories cannot resolve the same constitutive ambiguity.

The fixed cosine-storage premise is essential to that obstruction. The same cubic pressure has an all-degree completion if its phase potential is changed explicitly to

\[ U_\epsilon(\delta)=1-\cos\delta+ \epsilon\left(\frac23-\cos\delta+\frac{\cos^3\delta}{3}\right), \qquad \epsilon>0. \]

For c=cos(delta) this is (1-c)+epsilon*(1-c)^2*(c+2)/3>=0, with U_epsilon(0)=0. Moreover U_epsilon'=sin(delta)+epsilon*sin(delta)^3 and U_epsilon''(0)=1. On any admitted finite support define

\[ \widetilde S_i=\sum_{j\sim i}U_\epsilon'(\theta_j-\theta_i),\qquad g_i=\frac{\widetilde S_i}{\pi d_i},\qquad F_i=\frac{w\nu_iq_i}{\beta\pi d_i},\qquad E_\epsilon=E_D+\beta\sum_{\{i,j\}}U_\epsilon(\theta_j-\theta_i). \]

Then grad_theta E_epsilon=-beta*tilde S, so the same constant reciprocal Poisson tensor and form-diffusion block reproduce both rows, and dot E_epsilon=-e*q^T*N*D^-1*q. Odd edge currents preserve weighted form balance at positive held capacities. The pressure is smooth and pairwise, and its complete consensus Jacobian equals the normalized-sine one, although its nonlinear phase potential and pressure differ.

At the degree-three witness the original sine sum vanishes, but the changed phase gradient does not; the exchange therefore has the missing phase work. This countermodel shows why conservation, Jacobi, smoothness and the consensus response still do not select sine without a phase-storage premise. It changes that premise, rather than evading the fixed-cosine selection theorem. Cosine-storage capture certificates and the earlier native-pressure-derived storage classification cannot be transferred to it without checking their changed hypotheses. It supplies no new default law, runtime setting or physical storage identification.

docs.title: Exact local agreement does not select global winding passage
docs.text:
The restricted-domain classification already exhibits a smooth periodic addition invisible on acute gaps. The following complete-law comparison reuses that mechanism to test the specific C5 saddle preparation and retained connection. It is a constitutive counterexample, not a newly selected TNFR pressure or a rerun of that frozen response.

An explicit smooth continuation. Define

\[ c=\frac{\sqrt2}{2},\qquad y(\delta)=\frac{-\cos\delta-c}{1-c},\qquad h(y)=\begin{cases}0,&y\le0,\\ \exp(1-1/y),&y>0,\end{cases} \] \[ \boxed{U(\delta)=1-\cos\delta+2h(y(\delta)).} \]

The function exp(-1/y) and every derivative tend to zero at y=0+. Thus U is C-infinity, even, nonnegative and 2*pi-periodic, with U(0)=0, U''(0)=1 and U(pi)=4. Its added term and all its derivatives vanish for |wrap(delta)|<=3*pi/4. The associated odd edge current is

\[ j(\delta)=U'(\delta)= \begin{cases} \sin\delta,&y(\delta)\le0,\\ \displaystyle\sin\delta\left[1+ \frac{2\exp(1-1/y(\delta))}{(1-c)y(\delta)^2}\right],&y(\delta)>0. \end{cases} \]

This is smooth but not real analytic at the cutoff. Requiring global real analyticity together with exact equality on an open interval would exclude this continuation by analytic uniqueness. Such an analyticity requirement is an additional premise; it is not supplied by the nodal identity. Finite observations or equality of a finite number of derivatives would also be weaker than exact agreement on an open interval.

The complete law and its balance. On the same fixed simple unit graph, hold every capacity at one and take no forcing or events. In tau=t/pi, with K=diag(1/d_i) and q=Lx, declare

\[ S_{U,i}=\sum_{j\sim i}j(\theta_j-\theta_i),\qquad x'=KS_U,\qquad \theta'=Kq, \qquad H_U=\frac12x^{\mathsf T}Lx+\sum_{\{i,j\}}U(\theta_j-\theta_i). \]

The original-time rows are these rows divided by pi. In particular the supplied pressure is S_U/(pi*d), rather than a pressure reconstructed from the response. Since grad_theta H_U=-S_U,

\[ H_U'=q^{\mathsf T}KS_U-S_U^{\mathsf T}Kq=0. \]

Odd pair currents preserve both degree-weighted lifted origins. Periodic smoothness bounds j', so the full real-lift field is globally Lipschitz and has unique solutions in both time directions. Form reversal remains a reversing symmetry. These conclusions use the same constant reciprocal exchange construction as the preceding storage family. More generally its balance holds for an even C2 periodic potential with its derivative used as the current; nonnegative storage is a further hypothesis for the barrier below. This does not install an arbitrary-potential runtime or admit the changed law under the sine identifier.

Whole-window agreement for the actual preparation. Let the ideal near-saddle preparation be z_*+epsilon*(3X_lambda,-v_lambda), let r bound the actual rational center's full-coordinate error to it, and let delta be the independent preparation radius in every form and phase coordinate. The sine field has full maximum-norm Lipschitz constant two in scaled time. Its exact saddle is an equilibrium, and the ideal initial perturbation has norm at most 3epsilon. Hence for every |tau|<=3,

\[ \|z(\tau)-z_*\|_\infty \le e^6(3\varepsilon+r+\delta) < b:=729(3\varepsilon+r+\delta). \]

Every saddle edge has principal gap at most 2*pi/3. Therefore the strict check

\[ \boxed{2b<\frac\pi{12}} \]

keeps every cycle and contact edge in the region where both complete fields agree, throughout the window. Uniqueness transfers the entire trajectory there, rather than merely its initial derivatives. The nominal rational preparation consequently retains the same finite local directional gates. The independent full-state cube retains equality of the two flows; it does not acquire the nominal center's exact signed-family symmetry.

The original preparation uses epsilon=2^-32 and delta=2^-100. Its representation error must be rebuilt, and this stronger whole-window condition checked: an earlier, weaker phase-radius flag is insufficient. All initial edge additions then vanish exactly, so the full alternative storage equals the sine storage on the admitted preparation cube. Rebuild its upper enclosure and require H_U^upper<4. One independent sufficient check, with m full-support edges, is the sine-storage Taylor bound

\[ H_U(z+e)\le H_{\sin}(z) +\delta\left(\sum_i|(Lx)_i|+\sum_i|S_i|\right) +4m\delta^2, \qquad \|e\|_\infty\le\delta, \]

where the initial cube is wholly in the common-potential region. The two quadratic remainders use |e_j-e_i|<=2delta and |cos|<=1. For the present support m=10. Initial winding and branch admission remain separate from the storage test.

A different global outcome for the same preparation. Winding on a fixed cycle can change only when an edge meets its principal seam. At such a state that edge has potential U(pi)=4; every other potential and the form quadratic are nonnegative. Conservation and H_U<4 therefore forbid any seam, for all positive and negative time. An admitted initially winding-one cube remains winding one under this alternative.

The retained sine response instead reaches winding zero from that same intermediate preparation. No alternative trajectory is needed to decide this discriminator. The result does not prohibit formation from other preparations, establish permanent acute geometry, or show that the mapped sine winding-zero source fails under the alternative: that later source can have a different alternative storage. Local maintenance geometry and global accessibility are different obligations.

Which selection premises differ. The current remains additive over the full incident-gap multiset, but it cannot discard all information beyond the first resultant. Consider the two four-leaf stars with gap lists

\[ A=(5\pi/6,-\pi/6,0,0),\qquad B=(\pi/2,-\pi/2,0,0). \]

Both have degree four, Z_1=2 and zero sine sum. Set y_a=(sqrt(3)/2-c)/(1-c)>0. Only the first gap of A activates the addition, giving

\[ \sum_A j-\sum_B j=\frac{h(y_a)}{(1-c)y_a^2}>0, \qquad \sum_A U-\sum_B U=2h(y_a)>0. \]

Thus the first-moment sufficiency theorem excludes this law if its information restriction is independently required. At the first star's root, native argument pressure is zero while the alternative potential gradient is nonzero; all star resultants are regular. No finite diagonal metric can provide global alignment with the unchanged native pressure there. This is outside, rather than a counterexample to, the full-domain native-storage classification. Fixing cosine storage globally would likewise exclude the altered cost by premise.

The shared assess_saddle_storage_discriminator keeps this alternative's identity distinct, rebuilds the rational preparation and checks its common-region, full-storage and branch hypotheses. It is a detached static comparison: the input source anchors the support and reference law, rather than being relabeled as that generated preparation. Its local gate observations refer to the nominal preparation; its all-time winding exclusion consumes the separately admitted full cube. Neither it nor the existing classifications selects which global constitutive or information premise nature satisfies.

docs.title: What restricting primitive phase information selects
docs.text:
The alternative potential above leaves a precise information question: must the primitive phase source retain the whole incident-gap multiset, or can it discard everything except degree and the first complex circular moment? This is an additional constitutive premise, not a consequence of the nodal identity, reciprocity or the shared consensus tangent.

Let a bounded real kernel j(delta) be defined on the full phase circle; ordinary continuity suffices for boundedness. For any finite nonempty list of incident gaps, retain

\[ d=\#\{\delta_a\},\qquad Z_1=\sum_a e^{\mathrm i\delta_a},\qquad P=\sum_a j(\delta_a),\qquad g=P/(\pi d). \]

Here j is the unscaled edge current, so the preceding normalized edge kernel is j/pi. Repeated phases represent distinct neighboring nodes; simple stars realize these multisets without parallel edges. The information premise says that equal d,Z_1 imply equal P for all such lists. Degree is retained separately; this is not a direction-only Arg(Z_1) contract, and it does not add nonlocal data or future observations.

Classification. This premise holds if and only if

\[ \boxed{j(\delta)=c+a\cos\delta+b\sin\delta.} \]

If the edge current is odd, it follows that j(delta)=kappa*sin(delta). Consequently g=kappa*Im(Z_1)/(pi*d). The value of kappa still needs a normalization or constitutive scale; no coefficient is fitted to a response.

Elementary proof. Every point z of the closed disk |z|<=2 is the sum of two unit phasors. Degree-two sufficiency makes their current sum a well-defined function F_2(z), including different antipodal decompositions of zero. Comparing two degree-four lists gives

\[ F_2(z)+F_2(w)=F_2(z+w)+F_2(0) \quad\text{when }z,w,z+w\text{ lie in the disk}. \]

Thus G(z)=F_2(z)-F_2(0) is bounded and locally additive. If |z|<=2/n, additivity yields G(nz)=n*G(z); boundedness makes G continuous at zero. Integer subdivision, rational homogeneity and continuity give G(z)=a*Re(z)+b*Im(z) throughout the disk. Evaluating the repeated pair at z=2*exp(i*delta) yields the displayed classification, with c=F_2(0)/2. Conversely its sum is exactly cd+a*Re(Z_1)+b*Im(Z_1). Oddness eliminates the constant and cosine terms. No differentiability or pressure dynamics is used in this information theorem.

If the premise is initially restricted to lists with nonzero Z_1, two equal-zero lists can each be padded with one aligned entry. Their resultants become one and their degrees remain equal; canceling the common contribution proves the needed equality at zero. The same proof then applies. This comparison does not assign a direction or a native pressure at zero resultant. Degree two alone is insufficient to select sine. A nonzero resultant already determines its unordered pair of unit phasors; zero leaves the antipodal pair (delta,delta+pi) undetermined. Cancellation on every such pair requires the additional half-turn condition j(delta+pi)=-j(delta), not merely oddness j(-delta)=-j(delta). The non-sine cubic current above and sin(3*delta) satisfy both conditions and therefore pass every degree-two comparison. The classification also compares degree-four compositions; its premise ranges over all finite lists, not just pairs.

For example, j_2(delta)=sin(2*delta)/2 is odd, has unit consensus slope and derives from the even nonnegative potential U_2=sin(delta)^2/2. Nevertheless its sum on an antipodal pair is sin(2*delta), which depends on the unresolved orientation. Thus some odd currents can be distinguished already at degree two. For a smooth odd periodic current, half-turn antisymmetry removes the even sine harmonics; oddness alone does not. The all-degree information premise then removes the remaining higher harmonics. These are distinct restrictions on the supplied law, not interchangeable consequences of reciprocity or an even phase potential.

Storage consequence and independent premises. When the current is the derivative of a periodic potential, j=U', integrating the odd result and normalizing U(0)=0 gives U=kappa*(1-cos(delta)). Nonnegative storage requires kappa>=0; unit consensus curvature selects kappa=1. Alternatively, applying the classification directly to an even additive potential whose sum is determined by d,Z_1 gives the same normalized shape. These are conditional selection statements, not a derivation of first-moment sufficiency itself.

The two central premises are independent. Native argument pressure consumes the first resultant but is not an additive sum of one common edge current; the existing composition boundary retains that distinction. Conversely the smooth cubic-sine current is additive, odd and conservative under its supplied companion law, but consumes information beyond the first moment. The next control exposes exactly that discarded information, rather than merely comparing two unequal laws.

docs.title: Balanced geometry does not independently select the phase current
docs.text:
Consider the structural proposal that every finite phase neighborhood whose unit vectors sum to zero must exert zero net phase current:

\[ \sum_a e^{\mathrm i\delta_a}=0 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \sum_a j(\delta_a)=0. \tag{BC} \]

For a bounded additive odd kernel on the full phase circle, this proposal is equivalent to first-moment sufficiency, not an independent deduction of it. A two-member balanced list first gives \(j(\delta+\pi)=-j(\delta)\). For any equal-resultant lists \(A,B\), append the half-turn shift of \(B\) to \(A\). The combined resultant vanishes, so (BC) gives \(\sum_A j=\sum_B j\). Applying the preceding classification and oddness selects \(j(\delta)=\kappa\sin\delta\); conversely that current obeys (BC). Without oddness, (BC) permits a cosine term as well. It forbids the constant term which degree-aware first-moment sufficiency alone permits.

Thus calling the first phase resultant a geometric balance does not prove that it contains all the information used by pressure. The smooth cubic alternative above supplies an exact control. On the rotated balanced triad \(\delta_a=\pi/6+2\pi a/3,\ a=0,1,2\), both the resultant and sine sum vanish, but \(\sum_a\sin^3\delta_a=-3/4\). Its normalized phase pressure is therefore \(-\epsilon/(4\pi)\). Both complete smooth laws admit this configuration. The native argument-pressure law does not: its zero-resultant direction is undefined. This test does not extend that native domain by convention.

Checking only pairs and balanced triads is insufficient. For any \(\eta>0\),

\[ j_\eta(\delta)=\frac{\sin\delta+\eta\sin(5\delta)}{1+5\eta}, \qquad U_\eta(\delta)= \frac{1-\cos\delta+(\eta/5)(1-\cos(5\delta))}{1+5\eta} \]

is odd, has unit consensus slope, and derives from a nonnegative even potential. It cancels on every antipodal pair and every rotated balanced unit triad, but not on a regular pentagon rotated by \(\pi/10\): its current sum there is \(5\eta/(1+5\eta)>0\). A balanced unit triad is necessarily an equilateral phase arrangement; the fifth harmonic survives its symmetry. These are phase-space configurations, not physical spatial polyhedra. This counterexample is an algebraic admission control, not a new engine law.

The premise audit consequently closes with a nonselection result: (BC) is a meaningful candidate constitutive restriction, but its unrestricted version restates the information choice and its pair/triad version leaves other smooth conservative potentials. None of the nodal identity, reciprocity or existing persistence results establishes (BC). An independent structural principle or observation is still required.

docs.title: Equal first moments conceal a higher-harmonic response
docs.text:
Use phase turns and fix u=1/6. On a degree-three star, set the root phase to zero and compare leaf-gap lists

\[ A=(-u,u,\alpha),\qquad B=(0,\alpha-u,\alpha+u), \qquad 0<|\alpha|<1/12. \]

Both preparations have strictly acute edges. Their root resultants are nonzero with positive real part, and each degree-one leaf is also regular. Thus the whole supplied star is admitted; it need not be an equilibrium. For Z_k=\sum exp(2*pi*i*k*gap_turn), direct phasor algebra gives

\[ Z_1(A)=Z_1(B)=1+e^{2\pi\mathrm i\alpha},\qquad Z_3(A)-Z_3(B)=3(e^{6\pi\mathrm i\alpha}-1). \]

Since sin(delta)^3=(3*sin(delta)-sin(3*delta))/4, the existing j_epsilon=sin(delta)+epsilon*sin(delta)^3 has

\[ \boxed{g_\epsilon(A)-g_\epsilon(B) =-\frac{\epsilon\sin(6\pi\alpha)}{4\pi},\qquad \sum_AU_\epsilon-\sum_BU_\epsilon =\frac\epsilon4[\cos(6\pi\alpha)-1].} \]

Cosine storage and the sine root source agree between these lists. At the fixed choice alpha=1/24, the cubic differences are respectively -epsilon*sqrt(2)/(8*pi) and epsilon*(sqrt(2)-2)/8. Forms, capacities, coefficients and clock can be held identical on the same star; these are initial source and storage identities, not sampled future predictions or equilibrium certificates.

The shared phase-response reader provides PhaseMomentInformationAssessment through assess_phase_moment_information(left, right, epsilon=...). Its primitive inputs are exact rational unit phasors (cos(delta),sin(delta)), retaining first and third moments, both candidate sources and both potentials. It does not decode arbitrary roots of unity or install a new runtime law. One exact rational control uses three copies each of (1,0),(3/5,4/5) on the left, and five copies of (4/5,3/5) plus one (4/5,-3/5) on the right. Both have degree six and Z_1=(24/5,12/5). Their right-minus-left cubic source and storage differences are -14*epsilon/(125*pi) and -24*epsilon/125. The information controls retain exact equality and admission, alongside the existing composition controls. Such finite controls exercise this reader; the classification is the proof above, not an inference from those examples.

Scope under composition and observation. The stationary mediator result already gives a collective phase cost k-|Z_1|. This is nonpairwise but still a function of the first resultant. It therefore violates primitive edge additivity, not first-moment sufficiency by itself. Its retained finite capacity also brings memory and hidden initialization; that earlier proof must not be replaced by a claim that every coarse law needs higher harmonics.

Likewise, sufficiency for the root's instantaneous source or storage does not make d,Z_1 a sufficient full state or future predictor. Neighbor dynamics, form, capacities and hidden state retain their separate contracts. The result identifies what a primitive information restriction would select and what the known alternative retains. Why that restriction should hold fundamentally remains open; no physical selection, autonomous support mechanism or new default law follows.

docs.title: A finite observation of the information restriction
docs.text:
The existing exact degree-six preparations give a prospective test without reconstructing pressure from an evaluated derivative. For each preparation, use a seven-node star with fixed undirected unit support, unit held capacities, zero loss, unit phase weight and storage coefficient, and no inputs or events. Set all ideal forms to zero and the root phase to zero. The six leaf phasors are the rational lists above: three copies each of \((1,0),(3/5,4/5)\) for \(A\), and five copies of \((4/5,3/5)\) plus one \((4/5,-3/5)\) for \(B\). They have the same first resultant and degree. They need not have equal storage under the alternative law.

In the declared common clock \(\tau=t/\pi\), the complete supplied family is

\[ x_i'=\frac1{d_i}\sum_{j\sim i}j_\epsilon(\theta_j-\theta_i), \qquad \theta_i'=x_i-\frac1{d_i}\sum_{j\sim i}x_j, \qquad j_\epsilon(\delta)=\sin\delta+\epsilon\sin^3\delta. \]

The phase row and the associated \(U_\epsilon\) are retained from the complete storage family above. This is not a held-phase pressure experiment. Compare \(\epsilon=0\) with one prospectively fixed \(\epsilon>0\). The observation is the difference of the two root form readings at the same finite time \(h>0\), \(D_\epsilon(h)=x_{0,B}(h)-x_{0,A}(h)\). Its ideal initial derivative is \(-14\epsilon/125\).

Let \(J_\epsilon=1+\epsilon\) and \(L_\epsilon=1+3\epsilon\); these globally bound \(|j_\epsilon|\) and \(|j_\epsilon'|\). Admit independent initial errors of at most \(\rho\ge0\) in each form and lifted phase coordinate around each ideal preparation. The laws, capacities, support and clock are held exact. Then, on the full nonlinear star and for \(\tau\ge0\),

\[ |x_i(\tau)|\le\rho+J_\epsilon\tau,\qquad |\theta_i'(\tau)|\le2\rho+2J_\epsilon\tau, \] \[ |\delta_{ij}(\tau)-\delta_{ij}^{\rm ideal}(0)| \le 2\rho+4\rho\tau+2J_\epsilon\tau^2. \]

Integrating the Lipschitz bound on each root's phase current, including its initial form error, gives

\[ \left|x_0(h)-h\,\overline j_\epsilon^{\rm ideal}(0)\right| \le \rho(1+2L_\epsilon h+2L_\epsilon h^2) +\frac23L_\epsilon J_\epsilon h^3. \]

If each endpoint root reading additionally has error at most \(\sigma\ge0\), the measured difference belongs to

\[ \boxed{D_\epsilon^{\rm measured}(h)\in -\frac{14\epsilon h}{125}+[-R_\epsilon,R_\epsilon],\qquad R_\epsilon=2\rho(1+2L_\epsilon h+2L_\epsilon h^2) +\frac43L_\epsilon J_\epsilon h^3+2\sigma.} \]

These bounds use every node's evolving form and phase; no numerical trajectory, linearization or discarded leaf state enters the proof. Absolute current bounds give at most linear form growth and exclude finite-time escape, so the complete smooth solutions exist over the declared window. The bound is sufficient, not an optimized noise budget.

For the declared example \(\epsilon=1,h=1/16,\rho=\sigma=0\), the two prediction intervals are

\[ D_0\in[-1/3072,1/3072],\qquad D_1\in-7/1000+[-1/384,1/384]. \]

Their separation is \(521/128000\). Allowing the separately declared \(\rho=\sigma=1/100000\) still leaves the exact positive separation \(25453/6400000\), before outward numerical materialization. These are structural-coordinate budgets, not a claim about laboratory precision.

Equal initial information is not equal future response. Writing \(\mu=\operatorname{mean}_a j(\delta_a)\), the full zero-form star rows give \(\delta_a''(0)=-j(\delta_a)-3\mu\) and

\[ x_0'''(0)=\operatorname{mean}_a \big[j'(\delta_a)(-j(\delta_a)-3\mu)\big]. \]

For the sine member, the two values are \(-6/5\) and \(-32/25\). Consequently \(D_0'''(0)=-2/25\); in particular the future sine contrast is not identically zero. The finite error interval, rather than an assumed zero baseline, is what permits the law comparison.

The shared phase-response owner supplies assess_phase_information_response. It reuses exact phasor admission and the source comparison, propagates declared preparation/readout budgets and exports both predictions through the SDK. Exact unit phasors specify generally irrational ideal angles; floating angle conversion error belongs in the preparation budget. The controls compare independent full-star evolution and include inconclusive budgets. This report neither installs a law nor admits physical data. Disjoint predictions distinguish the two supplied models, not every possible kernel; agreement with a sine interval cannot prove universal first-moment sufficiency. Independent physical preparation, observation and clock identification remain the missing admission.

The finite receiver collision uses this same complete kernel family for a separate inverse question. One exact endpoint can coincide for different law coefficients and internal orientations; this does not contradict selection of sine when first-moment sufficiency is independently required.

docs.title: Phase information must retain its pairing with motion
docs.text:
The existing resultant chain rule already differentiates the first moment. Its higher-harmonic version connects the preceding static source comparison to response and work without adding a primitive coordinate or changing a law. On fixed support, let each relative gap have a declared angular rate r_a=dot(delta_a) in one specified clock, and define

\[ Z_m=\sum_a e^{\mathrm i m\delta_a},\qquad M_m=\sum_a r_a e^{\mathrm i m\delta_a},\qquad \boxed{\dot Z_m=\mathrm i m M_m.} \]

For the existing cubic-sine current, put A=1+3*epsilon/4 and B=epsilon/4. Its source and incident potential are pi*d*g=A*Im(Z_1)-B*Im(Z_3) and V_inc=d*(1+2*epsilon/3)-A*Re(Z_1)+(B/3)*Re(Z_3). Consequently

\[ \boxed{\pi\dot g= \frac{A\operatorname{Re}M_1-3B\operatorname{Re}M_3}{d}, \qquad \dot V_{\rm inc}=A\operatorname{Im}M_1-B\operatorname{Im}M_3.} \]

These identities assume fixed coefficients and support. The potential rate counts root incidences once; it is not a whole-network storage balance. Phase rates are supplied with their provenance or derived from the complete chosen law, never reconstructed from the source response being predicted.

A complete-law pairing control. On the three-node star 0--1,0--2, use unit capacity, e=0,w=beta=1 and the conservative sine law in tau=t/pi. Keep the labeled relative phasors fixed at (3/5,4/5) and (4/5,3/5) and compare

\[ x^{(A)}=(0,3/4,-1/4),\qquad x^{(B)}=(0,-1/4,3/4). \]

The full phase row theta'=D^{-1}Bx gives the common root rate -1/4 and the respective relative-rate lists (1,0) and (0,1), where B is the unnormalized graph Laplacian and primes here use tau. Both states have the same labeled phases, hence every unweighted circular moment, the same form and rate multisets, the same degree-weighted form mean 1/8 and the same full storage 73/80. Nevertheless

\[ x'_0(A)=x'_0(B)=7/10,\qquad x''_0(A)=3/10,\quad x''_0(B)=2/5, \] \[ V'_{\rm inc}(A)=4/5,\qquad V'_{\rm inc}(B)=3/5. \]

Thus even all phase moments together with a separate rate multiset discard information needed for the next response: which motion belongs to which phase. The example changes that association, not the pressure law. The different incident work is compatible with conservation of total storage.

The shared derive_phase_moment_motion returns PhaseMomentMotion from exact unit phasors and declared gap rates, reusing the static moment admission. The existing sine comparison's resultant_kinematics() derives its first-moment rates from rebuilt full-law state. The native joint-response owner instead consumes the argument-source Jacobian; its law must not be replaced by this sine or cubic derivative.

Retaining M_m still does not establish an autonomous reduction. Where the rates are differentiable,

\[ \dot M_m=\sum_a\dot r_a e^{\mathrm i m\delta_a} +\mathrm i m\sum_a r_a^2 e^{\mathrm i m\delta_a}. \]

Accelerations and further phase/rate correlations therefore enter unless an admitted invariant family or observation closure determines them. This is the same information-retention issue addressed by the existing complete-law and hidden-memory owners, not a reason to introduce free fitted moments.

There is a scoped sufficient-state exception, already connected to the unordered pair and its temporal reconstruction. For the same three-node star, the regular moment chart reconstructs the full relative state from (Z1,M1) when 0<|Z1|<2, and derives its exact evolution. It retains four real degrees of freedom; it does not close generic moment statistics. Coincident phases hide internal form variance. Antipodal phases with nonzero M1 retain the unordered phase pair but hide its mean form relative to the root. Those boundary controls are part of the same retained-state argument, not new primitive variables.

docs.title: Existing acute-star observations separate the premises
docs.text:
Reuse the preceding composition control's incident-gap preparation: a star with root phase zero and leaf phases (0,0,t), 0<t<pi/2. The balance control fixes t=1/2, x=(0,0,0,0), capacities (1,2,3,4) in root-first order, e=0, w=beta=1, no Gamma or events, and epsilon=1 for the current-squared comparison. The source laws, clock and exact preparation are declared before this static evaluation; no trajectory is acquired. Reuse of the earlier gaps is distinct from evaluating these whole-form observations. No earlier frozen response or producer is regenerated.

More generally, at uniform form and arbitrary positive held capacities, all three laws have zero phase velocity and zero instantaneous storage loss at this star. Their weighted-form mean rates nonetheless differ:

\[ \dot M_{\rm native} =\frac{w}{\pi W}\left[ 3\arctan\!\left(\frac{\sin t}{2+\cos t}\right)-t\right]<0, \qquad \dot M_{\rm sine}=0, \] \[ \dot M_{\rm current^2} =-\frac{8w\epsilon\sin^3t}{9\pi W}<0 \qquad(\epsilon>0). \]

The native sign is the already proved merger defect. For the existing current-squared family, the root contributes (1+epsilon*sin(t)^2/9)*sin(t)/pi to sum_i d_i*g_i, and the nonaligned leaf contributes -(1+epsilon*sin(t)^2)*sin(t)/pi. Their difference gives the displayed expression. These are exact conditional initial-rate identities; the shared static readers check represented-state observations and intervals separately. The comparison reuses the existing laws and preparation rather than installing a new dynamics or claiming physical selection from a computed response.

The composition controls exercise these balance and branching boundaries. Whole-graph form balance concerns the held-support continuous law. Changing degrees or capacities changes its weights, and hybrid events need their own jump accounting. The invariant is not identified with physical mass, energy or a substrate origin. The conservation-only equivalence concerns the gap-only information class; the induced-neighborhood extension also requires exact cosine exchange. Neither conclusion selects a universal law or changes the native runtime and retained evidence.

docs.title: 11.9 Form balance, common origins and the primitive information contract
docs.text:
The conservation premise in section 11.8 has different content on a relative state and on a primitive nodal law. Fix a connected simple unit graph with at least two nodes, held strictly positive capacities, the original clock and an unforced complete field

\[ F=\dot x=Np,\qquad p=-eD^{-1}Bx+wg(\theta),\qquad \dot\theta=H(x,\theta). \]
