docs.title: Same complete trajectories, weighted means and two invariant charts
docs.text:
Use the fixed finite connected simple unit central-contact graph of the composition owner, with \(m\ge2\) components and classes in \(\{1,2\}\). Write \(\mathsf D=\operatorname{diag}(d_{\rm fine})\), \(K=\mathsf D^{-1}\), \(A=KL\), and \(\|v\|_{\mathsf D}^2=v^{\mathsf T}\mathsf Dv\). Then \(A\) is self-adjoint and nonnegative in this norm and \(\|A\|_{\mathsf D}\le2\). All orthogonal projections below use this metric. The structural clock and coordinate units are fixed.

Let \(\Theta\) be the aligned collection of centered class twists. For the full trajectory write \(u=\theta-\Theta\); for the lifted surrogate write \(\widetilde u=o+T\bar y\), with the block lift \(T\) and the supplied component origins restored. Its form is \(\widetilde x=T\bar x\). The surrogate begins at zero form and at these origins; the actual trajectories begin at their uninterrupted formation images. Their difference, rather than two separate distances to equilibrium, is the object to be bounded.

The actual degree-weighted common means of each flow are constant, but may differ between the flows. Put

\[ \mu_x=\frac{\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}\mathsf D(x-\widetilde x)}{W}, \qquad \mu_\theta=\frac{\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}\mathsf D(u-\widetilde u)}{W}, \qquad W=18m+2|E|. \]

The exact source zero sums and endpoint norm bounds imply

\[ |\mu_x|,|\mu_\theta|\le \mu_*:=\frac{2|E|\epsilon}{W}. \tag{1} \]

Subtract only these global constant differences when applying spectral estimates. Individual component means remain dynamical. Because common form and phase shifts leave both fields unchanged, this centering changes neither the difference dynamics nor their forcing. Restore (1) in each final raw-coordinate error bound.

Require the original full-law contact radius and storage tests to pass. Let \(E_H\) be the retained upper bound on actual initial full storage excess; let \(c_r=\cos(4\pi/9+\sqrt2r)>0\) be its acute-chart curvature lower bound. The ideal surrogate has initial internal storage zero and bridge storage \(\sum_E[1-\cos(o_j-o_i)]\le E_H\). Its quotient radius is no greater than the actual-family radius bound. In the same chart its internal quadratic curvature is \(c_i=\cos(2\pi k_i/9)\ge c_r\), and its bridge curvature is at least \(c_r\). The composition owner's full-graph gap and first-exit proof therefore also trap the surrogate, using its own exact storage balance. This is an additional argument about that flow, not a transfer of full-law identity based solely on proximity at one time.

Both storages remain at most \(E_H\) above their respective critical values. Their nonnegative form terms and phase coercivity give, for every future time,

\[ \sum_{\rm fine\ edges}|\Delta u|^2\le\frac{2E_H}{c_r}, \qquad \sum_{\rm fine\ edges}|\Delta\widetilde u|^2 \le\frac{2E_H}{c_r}. \tag{2} \]

Here edge differences are deviations from the aligned twist, with its fixed closing-edge integers. Taylor's linear terms cancel because the reference is critical for the full joined graph. The bridge reference gaps are zero. Both charts use continuous lifts; no wrapping of real deviations is performed during this argument.

Set \(\beta_*=(2E_H/c_r)^{1/2}\). Admit the sharpened fixed floor

\[ \cos(4\pi/9+\beta_*)\ge c:=1/6. \tag{3} \]

Every edge deviation is bounded by \(\beta_*\), so (3) bounds the curvature along the reference-to-state segments for both flows and along each segment between their bridge gaps. Reapplying the phase energy estimate yields the useful edge budget

\[ B^2:=2E_H/c=12E_H,\qquad \sum|\Delta u|^2,\ \sum|\Delta\widetilde u|^2\le B^2. \tag{4} \]

This is not a node-phase norm bound. In particular, it does not lose another factor of the slow intercomponent spectral gap.

docs.title: Parity and independently admitted spectral gaps
docs.text:
Reflect each C9 by \(j\mapsto8-j\), fixing its central port. Let \(P_+,P_-\) be the blockwise even and odd projections. They are orthogonal in \(\mathsf D\), commute with \(A\), and preserve the global mean-free leaf. Every odd port value is zero. Contact incidence therefore annihilates odd vectors; the changed port degree has no effect on the odd block.

For each component the normalized odd diffusion block, in the four paired amplitudes, is the symmetric tridiagonal matrix with diagonal \((1,1,1,3/2)\) and off-diagonal entries \(-1/2\). Subtracting \(7I/30\) gives leading principal minors

\[ 23/30,\quad 76/225,\quad 1817/27000,\quad 323/405000, \]

all positive. Hence the uniform odd gap is \(\lambda_o=7/30\), independently of contacts and class.

The even gap must be admitted on the actual contact graph. Let \(\widehat L=T^{\mathsf T}LT\), \(M=T^{\mathsf T}\mathsf DT\), \(v=M\mathbf1\). A positive rational candidate \(q\le7/30\) is accepted only after the exact matrix inequality

\[ \widehat L-q\left(M-\frac{vv^{\mathsf T}}W\right)\succeq0. \tag{5} \]

It implies \(A\ge\lambda_e=q\) on the even global mean-free subspace. An unnormalized Laplacian gap cannot be inserted here unchanged. The frozen path uses \(q=3/100\); its finite rational PSD check is part of admission, not a fitted relaxation rate. An unsupported candidate must leave the corresponding all-time certificate unavailable.

docs.title: Difference dynamics keep the nonlinear coupling in explicit defects
docs.text:
Extend the surrogate to the fine space only as a proof device, retaining the class-linear internal currents and exact bridge sine currents. Its even subspace is invariant. For any full state \(z\), split the difference as

\[ F_{\rm full}(z)-F_{\rm sur}(\widetilde z) =[F_{\rm sur}(z)-F_{\rm sur}(\widetilde z)] +[F_{\rm full}(z)-F_{\rm sur}(z)]. \tag{6} \]

The first bracket uses the exact normalized averaged phase Hessian \(B_t\), namely \(K\) times the averaged Euclidean phase Hessian. Its internal weights are the constants \(c_i\), while each bridge weight is the integral of cosine along the segment between its two phase gaps. This operator is self-adjoint in the degree metric. By (3),

\[ cA\preceq B_t\preceq A,\qquad \|B_t\|_{\mathsf D}\le2. \tag{7} \]

All these operators commute with both parity projections. On each odd component \(B_t=c_iA\), although no commuting assumption is needed for the even estimate. Parity mixing remains in the second bracket of (6); the actual nonlinear sine field is not declared parity-invariant.

Let \(e=P_+u\), \(h=P_-u\). Orient the internal cycle edges consistently and use their fixed reference angle \(a=k_i2\pi/9\). Writing \(E_b=\Delta e\), \(H_b=\Delta h\) on an edge, reflection pairs its phase gap with the same \(H_b\) and opposite \(E_b\). The exact even and odd internal currents, after subtracting the constant reference current where necessary, are

\[ \cos(a+H_b)\sin E_b,\qquad \sin(a+H_b)\cos E_b-\sin a. \]

The surrogate currents are \(\cos(a)E_b\) and \(\cos(a)H_b\). Their residuals satisfy globally

\[ |r_{o,b}|\le\tfrac12(H_b^2+E_b^2),\qquad |r_{e,b}|\le |H_bE_b|+|E_b|^3/6. \tag{8} \]

The odd inequality splits the sine remainder in \(H_b\) from \(\sin(a+H_b)(\cos E_b-1)\). The even inequality splits the cosine change in \(H_b\) from the cubic sine remainder in \(E_b\). Thus it retains both hidden odd initialization and generated odd motion.

The internal incidence map obeys \(\|K\partial_{\rm int}^{\mathsf T}r\|_{\mathsf D} \le\sqrt2\|r\|_2\), because its squared norm is the largest normalized internal Laplacian eigenvalue, at most two. Even and odd internal edge vectors are orthogonal, so (4) bounds the sum of their squared norms. Equations (8) imply the time-independent odd forcing bound

\[ \|d_o(t)\|_{\mathsf D}\le D_o:=B^2/\sqrt2. \tag{9} \]

Once \(\|h(t)\|_{\mathsf D}\le O\) is established, use \(\|\Delta h\|_2\le\sqrt2O\), \(\max|E_b|\le B\), and \(\|\Delta e\|_2\le B\) to obtain

\[ \|d_e(t)\|_{\mathsf D}\le D_e:=2BO+\frac{\sqrt2}{6}B^3. \tag{10} \]

There is no circular closure: (9) follows from energy alone; it first gives \(O\), which then supplies (10). Bridge sine is exact and contributes no omitted-current defect.

docs.title: A forced mixed-coordinate estimate with initial-state exchange
docs.text:
For either centered parity difference, equations (6)--(7) are

\[ \delta x'=-A\delta x-\gamma B_t\delta u+\gamma d, \qquad \delta u'=\gamma A\delta x. \]

Set \(\eta=\gamma^2\), \(z=\gamma\delta x\), \(y=\delta u+z\). These are comparison coordinates, not new primitive state or a pressure reconstructed from response. They give

\[ y'=-\eta B_t(y-z)+\eta d,\qquad z'=-Az-\eta B_t(y-z)+\eta d. \tag{11} \]

Suppose this parity sector has gap \(\lambda\), and forcing norm at most \(D\). With \(Y=\|y\|_{\mathsf D}\), \(Z=\|z\|_{\mathsf D}\), (7) yields the upper right-derivative inequalities

\[ Y'\le-\eta c\lambda Y+2\eta Z+\eta D, \qquad Z'\le2\eta Y-(\lambda-2\eta)Z+\eta D. \tag{12} \]

They hold also at zero norms by their integral or Dini-derivative form. This is an estimate of trajectory differences under forcing; the earlier Lyapunov decay toward a fixed target was not applied to their difference.

Use positive interval endpoints \(\gamma_-\le\gamma\le\gamma_+\). In slow comparison time \(s=\eta(\tau-\tau_c)\), set

\[ a=c\lambda,\quad b=\lambda/\gamma_+^2-2,\quad \Delta_\lambda=ab-4,\quad C_\lambda=\begin{pmatrix}-a&2\\2&-b\end{pmatrix}. \]

Require \(\Delta_\lambda>0\). Then \(-C_\lambda\) has a positive inverse. If both initial centered form and phase norms are at most \(N\), define

\[ y_0=(1+\gamma_+)N,\quad z_0=\gamma_+N, \quad p=(-ay_0+2z_0)_+,\quad q_0=(2y_0-bz_0)_+. \]

The following rectangle retains possible initial exchange between channels:

\[ \begin{aligned} \mathcal Y(\lambda,D,N) &=y_0+\frac{b(D+p)+2(D+q_0)}{\Delta_\lambda},\\ \mathcal Z(\lambda,D,N) &=z_0+\frac{2(D+p)+a(D+q_0)}{\Delta_\lambda}. \end{aligned} \tag{13} \]

Indeed, its vector is \(r=(y_0,z_0)^{\mathsf T}+(-C_\lambda)^{-1} [D\mathbf1+(C_\lambda(y_0,z_0)^{\mathsf T})_+]\). It dominates the initial vector and satisfies \(C_\lambda r+D\mathbf1 =C_\lambda(y_0,z_0)^{\mathsf T} -(C_\lambda(y_0,z_0)^{\mathsf T})_+\le0\). The positive comparison system therefore cannot exit this rectangle. Neither initial channel norm is assumed individually monotone.

In particular, for all subsequent times,

\[ \|\delta u\|_{\mathsf D}\le\mathcal Y+\mathcal Z, \qquad \|\delta x\|_{\mathsf D}\le\mathcal Z/\gamma_-. \tag{14} \]

The second estimate may be conservative because its norm comparison does not retain every cancellation in the form response. It remains a valid enclosure; failure of a form-resolution test using it is not proof of a large actual form error.

docs.title: All-time parity bounds and separately resolved output channels
docs.text:
Let \(d_{\max}\) be the maximum contact degree. The admitted endpoint norms imply the conservative initial bounds

\[ N_o=\sqrt{2m}\,\epsilon,\qquad N_e=\sqrt{(2+d_{\max})m}\,\epsilon. \tag{15} \]

Odd port values vanish, so the odd degree metric is exactly two times the fine Euclidean metric. For even errors the largest fine degree is \(2+d_{\max}\). Parity projection and removal of the global weighted mean are orthogonal contractions, so they need no additional initial error inflation.

Apply (13) with \((\lambda_o,D_o,N_o)\), writing its outputs \((Y_o,Z_o)\), and put \(O=Y_o+Z_o\). The lifted surrogate is even, so this bounds the full odd phase itself. Insert that \(O\) in (10) and apply (13) with \((q,D_e,N_e)\), giving \((Y_e,Z_e)\). Both determinant conditions and all earlier basin, curvature, spectral and source premises must be admitted.

Since parity is orthogonal in the degree metric and each fine degree is at least two, the raw-coordinate bounds are

\[ \boxed{\begin{aligned} \mathcal E_\theta&=\mu_*+ \frac{\sqrt{(Y_o+Z_o)^2+(Y_e+Z_e)^2}}{\sqrt2},\\ \mathcal E_x&=\mu_*+ \frac{\sqrt{Z_o^2+Z_e^2}}{\gamma_-\sqrt2}. \end{aligned}} \tag{16} \]

They hold uniformly on \([\tau_c,\infty)\) for every actual admitted source member and every fine coordinate, relative to the same lifted surrogate. The mean floors in (1) have been restored exactly once. The argument does not compare independently chosen states on different mean leaves while silently setting their conserved differences to zero.

For fixed contact geometry and coefficients, \(E_H=O(\varphi^2+ \epsilon\varphi+\epsilon^2)\), \(D_o=O(E_H)\), and (13) yields \(O=O(E_H+\epsilon)\). Equation (10) is then \(O(E_H^{3/2}+\epsilon\sqrt{E_H})\). Thus the dominant all-time tracking error is of order \(\epsilon+\varphi^2\), rather than the order-\(\varphi\) sum of two unrelated distances to a target. The constants remain dependent on the admitted graph gaps and complete law. This order statement does not by itself certify either frozen channel allowance.

docs.title: Reporting and stopping boundary
docs.text:
For positive origin span \(\varphi\), the report admits separate fractions \(f_\theta,f_x\in(0,1]\), with allowances \(f_\theta\varphi\) and \(f_x\gamma\varphi\). The frozen control sets both fractions to \(1/2\). The form comparison uses the outward lower endpoint of its allowance. Each strict margin must itself have positive outward lower endpoint. A zero origin span supplies no positive resolution allowance; it does not turn a missing comparison into a passing flag.

Use exact rational gap admission and conservative outward upper bounds through (1)--(16). In particular, \(B^2=12E_H\) remains exact when forming \(D_o\) and \(B^3=B\,B^2\); an upper square-root bound for \(B\) is sufficient. Use upper \(\sqrt2\) for defect factors and lower \(\sqrt2\), \(\gamma\) for output denominators. The API's finite component cap is an implementation budget, not a theorem about a maximal number of components.

The all-time theorem requires both invariant charts, the energy bootstrap, the correct mean leaf and the two positive comparison determinants. Its certificates distinguish unavailable premises, proved uniform bounds, phase resolution and form resolution. Passing only the phase test cannot be described as all-channel predictive accuracy or as resolving a small contact-form signature. A failed sufficient bound is not an observed failure of either trajectory. The finite-window composition and earlier contact-response protocols remain unchanged.

docs.title: Reduced ports for actually formed sine classes
Prospective transfer claim and frozen protocol
docs.text:
The formed-class contact result establishes one finite donor-class response against receiver class one. This gate asks whether separately derived component models predict an additional contact against receiver class two, without refitting their parameters. The reduction retains five reflection-even spatial coordinates in each of two channels per component, an exact nonlinear bridge, and explicit bounds for all discarded fine-state effects. It is neither an exact nonlinear symmetry quotient nor a replacement of each component by one scalar form/phase pair.

Freeze the following before evaluating the held-out response:

  • Retain the complete positive-loss sine law, structural clock \(\tau=et\), \(e=1023/1024\), \(w=1/1024\), \(\gamma=1/(1023\pi)\), unit capacities and beta one. Two simple unit C9 cycles have local node order \(0,\ldots,8\). A single supplied unit bridge joins their central nodes \(4\); afterward the two port degrees are three and all other degrees two.
  • The donor cases remain \(k=1,2\); the held-out receiver is class \(\ell=2\) in both cases. For either component of class \(j\), retain source form \(jm(i-4)\), with \(m=(2046/9)(355/113)^2\). Donor nominal phases start at zero; receiver nominal phases start at the supplied common origin \(\varphi=1/1000\). This offset is a preparation premise, not a rotation or reset performed at contact.
  • Each component retains initial form and continuous phase-lift residual bounds \(10^{-10}\), with each residual row summing to zero separately. All allowed even and odd perturbations remain. Retain each component's original common storage ceiling \(10^9\); the nominal preparation costs need not agree. Both full source families, including the receiver-class-two source, must be freshly admitted under the original formation theorem.
  • Retain acquisition time \(100\), radius \(r=1/12\), and the uninterrupted unprobed relaxation duration \(D=10^{13}\). Contact occurs at \(\tau_c=100+D\). Retain the endpoint Euclidean bounds \(\epsilon=10^{-32}\) separately for each component's form and phase error, proved with the guarded exact decay bound \(2^{-512}\) and \(512\le\kappa D\le4096\). No target reset or previous maintenance probe is admitted.
  • Derive one component matrix for each class directly from its C9 geometry and the declared one-contact mobility. Retain the radial order \((4),(3,5),(2,6),(1,7),(0,8)\), in form and in real phase deviations from that class's fixed twist. The class dependence is \(\cos(2\pi j/9)\), derived from the internal sine field. Use these same two component matrices and the same two-channel port convention in every composition; no receiver-specific parameter or response fit is admitted.
  • The predictive system has twenty retained coordinates, ten per component. Its internal phase field is the derived linear tangent, while its bridge sine current remains exact and nonlinear. Retain the initial-state source term in the port representation. For the nominal prediction, use the limiting comparison coordinates and enclose the actual source deviations through the proved error terms; never reset the actual fine state.
  • At elapsed scaled time \(h=1/100\) after contact, read actual receiver-port form with independent additive error at most \(d=10^{-30}\) per case. Predict recorded donor-two minus donor-one contrast greater than \(10^{-25}\). Derive its fourth-order leading term from the composed reduced matrices, retaining their first three derivative cancellations. Do not substitute a coefficient or verdict from the earlier full-state contact certificate.
  • Bound the finite reduced prediction by its correlated semigroup tail and reduced nonlinear remainder. Add the separately proved lifted-surrogate discrepancy, complete actual preparation error and independent readout error. Let \(E_{\mathrm{total}}\) be the sum of these nonnegative error bounds and let \(L_{\mathrm{full}}\) be the lower endpoint of the final outward recorded-contrast enclosure. Require \(L_{\mathrm{full}}>10^{-25}\) and the strict error-fraction condition \(E_{\mathrm{total}}<(1/4)L_{\mathrm{full}}\). The denominator is a certified full-law recorded gap, not its formal leading amplitude.
  • Retain the supplied contact-work allowance \(10^{-6}\), both actual cycle identities and full joined-family recovery. Rebuild the contact storage, quotient radius, weighted means and barrier for donor \(k\) and receiver two. Removing the bridge must leave receiver evolution independent of donor data; retain the preparation/readout control band.
  • Use exact rational primitives and outward dyadic128 trigonometric intervals, keeping the tiny warmup squared bounds as exact rationals. Preserve the protocol and producing source before the first reserved evaluation. There is no trajectory integration, parameter search, new horizon sweep or precision search. If any prerequisite, error fraction, identity, work or contrast condition fails, retain that outcome without changing this protocol.

The earlier receiver-one result is a retained reference, not a calibration dataset for these component matrices. The new question is the controlled transfer of a derived reduced model to one declared receiver change. The structural dwell, initial source control and tiny readout budget have no independent laboratory realization here.

docs.title: The retained component state and one-contact normalization
docs.text:
Use local reflection \(R:i\mapsto8-i\), fixing the central port \(p=4\). For each channel, let \(S\) take the values or averages on the five layers

\[ (4),\quad(3,5),\quad(2,6),\quad(1,7),\quad(0,8). \]

Let \(T\) lift a five-vector by assigning its value to each node in its layer. Then \(ST=I_5\) and \(TS=(I+R)/2\). Both maps are contractions in the maximum norm. The reduced state is \(z_k=(\bar x_k,\bar y_k)\in\mathbb R^{10}\), where \(\bar x_k=Sx_k\) and \(\bar y_k=S(\theta_k-\Theta_k-o_k\mathbf1)\). Here \(\Theta_{k,i}=k\alpha(i-4)\), \(\alpha=2\pi/9\), and the declared common origin \(o_k\) is zero for the donor and \(\varphi\) for the receiver. This projection defines retained coordinates of a fine state. Evolving equation (2) instead defines a surrogate trajectory, which generally differs from the projection of the evolving nonlinear fine state.

The phase deviations are real retained lifts. Wrapping them before applying the internal linear operator changes this model. The internal reference twist and known origins must be restored when forming a circular bridge difference.

The component has one admitted unit contact. Its internal mobility is \(K_*=\operatorname{diag}(1/2,\ldots,1/3\text{ at }p,\ldots,1/2)\), even though \(L_{\mathrm{C9}}\) contains only its internal edges. Its reduced internal operator is

\[ \bar A=SK_*L_{\mathrm{C9}}T= \begin{pmatrix} 2/3&-2/3&0&0&0\\ -1/2&1&-1/2&0&0\\ 0&-1/2&1&-1/2&0\\ 0&0&-1/2&1&-1/2\\ 0&0&0&-1/2&1/2 \end{pmatrix}. \tag{1} \]

The edge joining nodes zero and eight lies inside the outermost layer and contributes zero on reflection-even vectors. The layer weights are \((3,4,4,4,4)\), of total nineteen. This is not the isolated-cycle normalization \(L_{\mathrm{C9}}/2\). A different number or arrangement of contacts would require its own mobility and reduction admission.

Every internal edge of the class-\(k\) twist has cosine \(c_k=\cos(k\alpha)>0\). Linearizing only those internal sine currents gives the following component model:

\[ \begin{aligned} \bar x_k'&=-\bar A\bar x_k-\gamma c_k\bar A\bar y_k +\frac{e_0}{3}(u_x+\gamma u_\theta),\\ \bar y_k'&=\gamma\bar A\bar x_k-\frac{\gamma e_0}{3}u_x. \end{aligned} \tag{2} \]

The two input channels have the definite convention

\[ u_x=x_{\mathrm{other},p}-x_{\mathrm{own},p},\qquad u_\theta=\sin(\theta_{\mathrm{other},p}-\theta_{\mathrm{own},p}). \]

They are not two unspecified forces. In the actual composition they are determined by the other component's retained port outputs.

For \(z_k=(\bar x_k,\bar y_k)\), define

\[ J_k= \begin{pmatrix} -\bar A&-\gamma c_k\bar A\\ \gamma\bar A&0 \end{pmatrix},\qquad B=\frac13 \begin{pmatrix} e_0&\gamma e_0\\ -\gamma e_0&0 \end{pmatrix},\qquad Cz_k=(\bar x_{k,0},\bar y_{k,0}). \]

The exact input/output identity for this component model is

\[ Cz_k(t)=Ce^{J_kt}z_k(0) +\int_0^t Ce^{J_k(t-s)}B\,u_k(s)\,ds. \tag{3} \]

Thus \(G_k(t)=Ce^{J_kt}B\) is its derived two-channel port kernel. It depends on class, supplied law and contact normalization, not on a fitted receiver response. The initial-state term is essential: the kernel does not determine the initial internal shape.

The twenty-coordinate realization retains both component means. Writing \(m_*=(3,4,4,4,4)^{\mathsf T}\), equation (1) gives

\[ (m_*^{\mathsf T}\bar x_k)'=u_x+\gamma u_\theta,\qquad (m_*^{\mathsf T}\bar y_k)'=-\gamma u_x. \]

Opposite inputs on the two components preserve the combined degree-weighted charges, while the separate component means can change. Holding them independently fixed after contact would introduce a different law.

This is a strict reduction from thirty-six fine coordinates to twenty retained coordinates, or an equivalent port history with its initial source. No minimality theorem is asserted. In particular, writing a kernel is not evidence that all hidden initialization can be discarded or that one scalar state per formed class closes the dynamics.

docs.title: Autonomous composition keeps the bridge nonlinear
docs.text:
Compose the two component models using

\[ \begin{aligned} u_{\mathrm D} &=\left(\bar x_{\mathrm R,0}-\bar x_{\mathrm D,0},\ \sin(\varphi+\bar y_{\mathrm R,0}-\bar y_{\mathrm D,0})\right),\\ u_{\mathrm R}&=-u_{\mathrm D}. \end{aligned} \tag{4} \]

The resulting twenty-coordinate system is autonomous after the supplied support event. No observed response is installed as an input, and no port is held to an externally selected future history. Only the choice \(\ell=2\) of the receiver's already defined component matrix changes in the held-out experiment.

Put

\[ \bar D=\operatorname{diag}(\bar A,0),\quad \bar R=\operatorname{diag}(0,\bar A),\quad q=e_0-e_5,\quad \bar C_b=qq^{\mathsf T}/3,\quad \bar A^+=\bar D+\bar R+\bar C_b. \]

In ten-component vectors \(\bar x,\bar y\), (2)--(4) become

\[ \begin{aligned} \bar x'&=-\bar A^+\bar x -\gamma(c_k\bar D+c_\ell\bar R)\bar y +\frac{\gamma q}{3} \sin(\varphi+\bar y_5-\bar y_0),\\ \bar y'&=\gamma\bar A^+\bar x. \end{aligned} \tag{5} \]

The first row is linear in the internal deviations but not in the bridge phase difference. Replacing that sine by a fitted gain or by its initial value would be another approximation requiring an additional error term.

docs.title: Why the discarded nonlinear modes remain controlled
docs.text:
The exact fine sine law does not preserve this even subspace in general. Around a winding-\(k\) twist, an internal edge contributes

\[ \sin(k\alpha+\delta) =\sin(k\alpha)+c_k\delta+O(\delta^2). \]

The terms proportional to \(\sin(k\alpha)\delta^2\) can generate reflection-odd deviations under an even drive. Linear reflection symmetry alone cannot prove an exact nonlinear quotient.

For the error proof, extend (5) to all nine coordinates of each component: use the linearized internal \(c_kK_*L_{\mathrm{C9}}\) and the exact bridge sine, without projecting either channel. This thirty-six-coordinate surrogate is a proof device. Its matrices commute with each component reflection and its bridge depends only on the fixed ports. Its ideal initial deviations are zero, so its ideal flow stays even and is exactly the lift of (5). The actual predictive realization remains twenty-dimensional.

Compare this lifted ideal surrogate to the ideal full sine flow with the same zero form and target twists plus receiver origin \(\varphi\). Let \(y_{\mathrm{fine}}(t)\) be phase displacement from those initial comparison phases and put \(s=|\sin\varphi|\). The complete joined field has initial normalized sine forcing \((\sin\varphi/3)(e_a-e_b)\), irrespective of \(k,\ell\). The contraction/Volterra argument in the contact remainder proof uses only this forcing, the normalized row bounds and \(\eta=\gamma^2\). It therefore applies with receiver class two:

\[ \|y_{\mathrm{fine}}(t)\|_\infty \le\frac{2\gamma^2s}{3}t^2 \quad(0\le t\le h\le1,\ \gamma^2h^2\le3/4). \tag{6} \]

At the actual fine phase state, the omitted internal Taylor terms have normalized magnitude at most \(2\|y_{\mathrm{fine}}\|_\infty^2\). They enter the physical form row multiplied by \(\gamma\) and do not directly enter the phase row. Both the full field and the extended surrogate have maximum-norm Lipschitz constant at most \(2+2\gamma<3\). Thus for \(0<h<1/3\), their full-state discrepancy obeys

\[ E_{\mathrm{sur}}(h) \le\frac{2\gamma}{1-3h} \int_0^h\|y_{\mathrm{fine}}(t)\|_\infty^2\,dt \le\frac{8\gamma^5s^2h^5}{45(1-3h)}. \tag{7} \]

Taking the supremum in the integral difference inequality proves the denominator: \(E_h\le3hE_h+\int_0^h\|\mathrm{defect}\|\,dt\). The same argument applies to every prefix of the window. Generated odd modes and their subsequent feedback are included through the full fine trajectory in (6), not set to zero.

For each actual formation image, arbitrary initial even and odd errors remain within the endpoint bound \(\epsilon\). Comparison of the actual full flow to the ideal full flow gives the separate maximum-norm bound

\[ E_{\mathrm{prep}}^{\mathrm{one}}(h) \le\frac{\epsilon}{1-3h}. \tag{8} \]

This is precisely the complete-field argument in the actual-state contact handoff. Combining (7) and (8) bounds the actual receiver form against the nominal reduced flow without resetting any actual coordinate. Unknown initial shape is handled by a proved family enclosure, not inferred from winding, means or port values alone.

docs.title: A finite prediction computed from the reduced matrices
docs.text:
The analytic evaluator of (5) starts with \(\bar x=\bar y=0\). Put

\[ f=\frac{\sin\varphi}{3}q,\qquad \bar B_{k,\ell}=c_k\bar D+c_\ell\bar R+\cos\varphi\,\bar C_b. \]

Direct differentiation of the reduced rows gives

\[ \begin{aligned} \bar x'&=\gamma f,\\ \bar x''&=-\gamma\bar A^+f,\\ \bar x'''&=\gamma(\bar A^+)^2f -\gamma^3\bar B_{k,\ell}\bar A^+f,\\ \bar x''''&=-\gamma(\bar A^+)^3f +\gamma^3\left( \bar A^+\bar B_{k,\ell}\bar A^+ +\bar B_{k,\ell}(\bar A^+)^2\right)f. \end{aligned} \tag{9} \]

The receiver is reduced coordinate five. Because its row of \(\bar D\) vanishes, the two donor cases have identical receiver derivatives through order three. Their fourth derivative is obtained from the rational reduced matrices through

\[ \begin{aligned} \chi_4&=-e_5^{\mathsf T} \left(\bar A^+\bar D\bar A^+ +\bar D(\bar A^+)^2\right)(q/3),\\ \Delta\bar Y''''(0)&=\chi_4\gamma^3\sin\varphi\,(c_1-c_2). \end{aligned} \tag{10} \]

For example, (1) gives \((\bar A^+q)_0=4/3\), \((\bar A^+q)_1=-1/2\), and \((\bar D\bar A^+q)_0=11/9\). The receiver bridge entry is \(-1/3\), so \(\chi_4=11/81\). This value is derived by composing the reduced operators. It is not a copied parameter from the earlier contact report. The changed receiver class also changes the individual derivative rows in (9), even though it cancels from this donor contrast.

Let \(d_c=c_1-c_2>0\). The exact reduced leading expression is

\[ P=\frac{\chi_4}{24}\gamma^3\sin\varphi\,d_c\,h^4. \tag{11} \]

Its finite response is not identified with this derivative alone. The normalized joined matrix \(\bar A^+\) has a contracting nonnegative semigroup, and \(\|\bar A^+\|_\infty,\|\bar D\|_\infty\le2\). The correlated first-\(\gamma^2\) semigroup expansion has the receiver terms

\[ e_5^{\mathsf T}\sum_{p,q\ge0} \frac{(-1)^{p+q}(\bar A^+)^p\bar D(\bar A^+)^{q+1}f} {(p+q+3)!}\,h^{p+q+3}. \]

All \(p=0\) terms vanish. Bounding the \(n=p+q\ge2\) tail uses \(n\) terms and successive ratio at most \(h/2\). Restoring the physical factors gives

\[ E_{\mathrm{tail}} =\frac{4s\,d_c\gamma^3h^5}{45(1-h/2)}. \tag{12} \]

This derives the tail from the reduced rows and their shared forcing, rather than subtracting two unrelated marginal estimates.

The reduced bridge remainder has normalized Taylor bound at most \(2\|\bar y\|_\infty^2\); this deliberately conservative bound also covers the sharper bridge-only constant. The same Volterra bootstrap used for (6), now on the reduced rows, bounds the paired nonlinear evaluation remainder by

\[ E_{\mathrm{nl}}=\frac{8s\gamma^5h^5}{15}. \tag{13} \]

Equations (12)--(13) bound the finite reduced-flow contrast around (11). Equation (7) has a different responsibility: it bounds the reduced-flow approximation to the original nonlinear fine law. Neither error can stand in for the other.

docs.title: Recorded transfer criterion and actual joined identities
docs.text:
Use independently admitted errors in both donor comparisons. An upper bound for the total error around the exact expression \(P\) is

\[ \begin{aligned} E_{\mathrm{total}}={}& E_{\mathrm{tail}}+E_{\mathrm{nl}} +\frac{16\gamma^5s^2h^5}{45(1-3h)} +\frac{2\epsilon}{1-3h}+2d. \end{aligned} \tag{14} \]

The five terms retain finite reduced evaluation, omitted nonlinear fine-state effects, arbitrary initial preparation error and independent observation error. No unknown error correlation is used to reduce this sum.

The implementation encloses \(P\) and forms the outward interval for \(P+[-E_{\mathrm{total}},E_{\mathrm{total}}]\), using outward upper bounds for every error term. Let \(L_{\mathrm{full}}\) be its final lower endpoint. The strict frozen rule is

\[ L_{\mathrm{full}}>10^{-25},\qquad E_{\mathrm{total}}<\tfrac14L_{\mathrm{full}}. \tag{15} \]

An outward enclosure of the fraction margin must also retain a strictly positive lower endpoint. Consequently rounding a positive exact margin to zero yields an unavailable certificate. The relevant denominator is the final recorded gap; neither a plotted midpoint nor the formal leading term can replace it.

The fixed analytic design has room for this extra obligation. Before interval rounding, at \(h=1/100\),

\[ \frac{E_{\mathrm{tail}}}{P} =\frac{1728}{10945}<\frac4{25}. \]

The bounds \(1/4000<\gamma<1/3000\), \(d_c>1/2\), \(1/2000<s<1/1000\), with the frozen \(\epsilon,d\), bound the other terms in (14) by less than \(P/1000\). Therefore

\[ E_{\mathrm{total}}<P/6,\qquad \frac{E_{\mathrm{total}}}{P-E_{\mathrm{total}}}<1/5<1/4. \]

The same coarse bounds give \(P>(1.5625)\,10^{-25}\), so \((5/6)P>10^{-25}\). These sufficient analytic inequalities select no new horizon, offset or precision. The reserved evaluation must still verify its actual outward endpoints and all prerequisite admissions.

The original formation theorem covers both classes separately. Receiver two uses its own freshly derived class-two source bounds; the common worst-class Lyapunov estimate gives the same \(\epsilon\) handoff after the declared unprobed dwell. The support and port normalization are unchanged, and both internal twists have edge magnitude at most \(4\pi/9\). Thus the full joined proof applies after explicitly replacing the receiver-one twist by receiver two. In particular it again gives

\[ Z^2\le4\epsilon^2+\frac92\varphi^2,\qquad H-H^*\le10\epsilon^2+\frac12(\varphi+2\epsilon)^2, \]

against the barrier \(r^2/1620\), and work bound \(2\epsilon^2+(\varphi+2\epsilon)^2/2\). The complete actual families retain winding pairs \((1,2)\) and \((2,2)\), respectively, with recovery on their actual postevent weighted-mean leaves. These are full-law claims with matched hypotheses; they do not follow merely from the reduced output error.

The joined weighted means remain those of the actual nodal values, with total weight thirty-eight. The class-two receiver's internal twist still has zero weighted mean by reflection. The degree reweighting, positive supplied event work and disconnected control bound \(2\epsilon/(1-3h)+2d\) therefore retain their original formulas. No report from the earlier receiver-one experiment supplies a cached passing verdict for this new instance.

docs.title: Interpretation and limits of the component law
docs.text:
The new claim is conditional predictive reuse: the same independently derived class matrices and exact bridge convention are composed with a different receiver, with a uniform finite error for actual formed families. The model does not discard memory by definition. Equation (3) retains its initial-state source and the dynamics of its internal even coordinates; equations (7)--(8) retain the effects of omitted odd and uncertain initial coordinates.

The finite derivative expansion is one certified evaluation of this reduced dynamical model. It is not a substitute for defining the model's retained state, port feedback and initialization. An insufficient error bound would not itself disprove that a useful reduction exists; an actual response outside a claimed enclosure would instead challenge its premises or proof.

The positive-loss microscopic law, source preparation, contact normalization and work remain supplied. The very long structural warmup and small readout budget are still mathematical premises. No minimal realization, universal constituent law, autonomous contact selection or physical sensor interpretation follows.

The shared reduced-port owner implements evaluate_sine_reduced_class_ports as a detached instantaneous evaluation of the twenty-coordinate field, and assess_sine_reduced_class_ports as its primitive-only finite certificate. The latter rebuilds the same matrices, computes the individual derivative rows and contrast coefficient, and consumes freshly derived formation and contact bounds. It accepts no incoming report as evidence and does not integrate a reduced or full trajectory. The contract and independent controls retain admission, error-budget and usage boundaries.

docs.title: Degree-aware composition of reduced sine-class ports
Prospective composition claim and frozen protocol
docs.text:
The two-component reduction admits one central contact per component. This gate asks whether the derived component description composes on a finite simple undirected unit contact graph, with the actual contact degrees, an exact joined storage balance and a uniform finite-window approximation of the complete fine law. It does not ask for another donor-class response comparison.

Freeze this single control before evaluating its certificate:

  • Use three simple unit C9 components, in component order \((0,1,2)\) and local node order \(0,\ldots,8\), with winding classes \((1,2,1)\). The supplied contact edges are \((0,1)\) and \((1,2)\), each joining the local central nodes \(4\). Their contact degrees are \((1,2,1)\); the joined fine port degrees are \((3,4,3)\).
  • Retain unit capacities, beta one, \(e=1023/1024\), \(w=1/1024\), the structural clock \(\tau=et\), and \(\gamma=1/(1023\pi)\). The complete rows on each live support are

[ x'=-KLx+\gamma KS(\theta),\qquad \theta'=\gamma KLx, ]

where \(K\) is inverse fine degree, \(L\) is the unit Laplacian, and \(S_a(\theta)=\sum_{b\sim a}\sin(\theta_b-\theta_a)\). No edge weights, loss changes, inputs or occurrence law are inferred. - Retain the original class-specific form sources \(k_i m(j-4)\), \(m=(2046/9)(355/113)^2\). Nominal initial phases are constant on each component, with supplied origins \((o_0,o_1,o_2)=(0,1/1000,0)\). Each component has independent per-coordinate initial form and continuous phase-lift errors at most \(10^{-10}\), subject to zero sum separately in each channel. Retain all sixteen relative source coordinates per component and its original storage ceiling \(10^9\); source costs need not agree. - Freshly admit formation of both classes at \(\tau=100\) and relative radius \(r=1/12\). Continue the actual unprobed trajectories for \(D=10^{13}\). Require Euclidean form and target-phase error bounds \(\epsilon=10^{-32}\), separately on every component, using the exact decay bound \(2^{-512}\) only if \(512\le\kappa D\le4096\). The original common origins are retained; no target reset is made. - At \(\tau_c=100+D\), add the two unit contacts simultaneously, leaving every state coordinate unchanged. Declare total event-work allowance \(2\,10^{-6}\), the sum of two declared per-edge allowances. Hold the joined support and complete law afterward. Require full joined-family acute identity retention and recovery on its actual postevent conserved-mean leaf. - Derive the thirty-coordinate surrogate, ten coordinates per component, from the actual postcontact degrees. Retain the class tangent only for internal cycle currents and the exact nonlinear bridge currents. The full comparison has fifty-four coordinates. The nominal surrogate starts at zero form and zero displacement from the limiting twists and supplied origins; actual fine-state errors remain in the approximation bound, not in a reset. - Require the maximum absolute error in each fine form and phase coordinate, relative to the lifted surrogate, to stay strictly below \(2\epsilon=2\,10^{-32}\) throughout \(0\le\tau-\tau_c\le h=1/100\). This is a full-state mathematical approximation allowance in the fixed normalized coordinate units, not a sensor error or a new response contrast. - Retain the exact degree-normalization control: with all phase deviations and origins zero, middle port form one and every other retained form zero, the middle form rate is \(-1\). Reusing the one-contact denominator three gives \(-4/3\) and a nonzero actual-degree-weighted form-charge rate \(-4/3\). Require the degree-aware assembly's exact storage/loss and charge identities, rather than a tolerance-based pass for this rational control. - Preserve source and protocol before the first reserved control evaluation. Use admitted exact primitives and outward rational interval bounds. Keep the tiny squared handoff bounds and decay as exact rationals. No trajectory integration, topology search, horizon/precision sweep or refitted component coefficient is admitted. Pass only if fresh formation, every actual handoff, contact work, full identity, algebraic controls and the strict whole-window approximation allowance all pass unchanged.

The reusable theorem below concerns fixed finite simple undirected unit central-contact graphs. It does not extend the law to weighted support, arbitrary port locations or changing contacts during the certified window. Supplying contacts and organized sources does not derive their occurrence. The long structural dwell and source accuracy have no laboratory bridge.

docs.title: Component coordinates, contact degree and origins
docs.text:
Let \(\mathcal G\) be a fixed finite simple undirected unit graph on \(m\) components. Give component \(i\) class \(k_i\in\{1,2\}\), contact degree \(d_i\), and one declared real common phase origin \(o_i\). Each contact joins the central nodes, so it changes only their fine degrees, from two to \(2+d_i\). With \(\alpha=2\pi/9\), use the centered reference twist \(\Theta_{i,j}=k_i\alpha(j-4)\) and \(c_i=\cos(k_i\alpha)>0\).

Use the reflection projection and lift \(S,T\) on the five layers \((4),(3,5),(2,6),(1,7),(0,8)\). They obey \(ST=I_5\), \(TS=(I+R)/2\), and have maximum-norm operator norm one. For a fine state, the coordinate map is

\[ \bar x_i=Sx_i,\qquad \bar y_i=S(\theta_i-\Theta_i-o_i\mathbf1). \]

The reduced trajectory defined below is a surrogate, generally different from the projection of an evolving nonlinear fine state. Its lifted phase is \(\Theta_i+o_i\mathbf1+T\bar y_i\). In particular, the common origin is not also included in \(\bar y_i\).

Let \(L_0=2L_{P_5}\), twice the five-node path Laplacian. The edge between fine nodes zero and eight has zero difference on an even lift. The exact reduced mobility mass and internal operator are

\[ M_i=T^{\mathsf T}\operatorname{diag}(d_{\rm fine})T =\operatorname{diag}(2+d_i,4,4,4,4),\qquad A_i=M_i^{-1}L_0. \tag{1} \]

Thus the first row of \(A_i\) is \((2,-2,0,0,0)/(2+d_i)\). The other four rows are unchanged from the one-contact reduction. The class coefficient is inherited from the cycle; mobility additionally depends on the declared interface. Treating the one-contact matrix as independent of contact degree would change the complete law, rather than reuse its reduction.

For each component aggregate the two definite input channels

\[ u_{x,i}=\sum_{j\sim i}(\bar x_{j,0}-\bar x_{i,0}),\qquad u_{\theta,i}=\sum_{j\sim i} \sin(o_j-o_i+\bar y_{j,0}-\bar y_{i,0}). \]

With \(e_0\) the central layer vector, the component equations are

\[ \begin{aligned} M_i\bar x_i'&=-L_0\bar x_i-\gamma c_iL_0\bar y_i +e_0(u_{x,i}+\gamma u_{\theta,i}),\\ M_i\bar y_i'&=\gamma L_0\bar x_i-\gamma e_0u_{x,i}. \end{aligned} \tag{2} \]

Both rows use the same postcontact degree. The state has ten coordinates per component rather than eighteen. Disconnected contact graphs and an isolated component also define these equations; a single global recovery certificate will separately require connected support.

All edge origins must come from the same vector \(o\). Their signed sum around every contact cycle is zero as a real lift. Independent edge offsets with a nonzero cycle sum would introduce a different frustrated model. Common shifts of all \(o_i\) are immaterial to rates. Replacing \(o_i\) by \(o_i+a_i\) and \(\bar y_i\) by \(\bar y_i-a_i\mathbf1\) preserves each reconstructed phase and all rates, since \(L_0\mathbf1=0\). Wrapping arbitrary phase deviations before applying \(L_0\) is not this coordinate change.

docs.title: Exact assembled storage, dissipation and charges
docs.text:
Stack the retained vectors, set \(M=\operatorname{diag}(M_i)\), and let \(b_{ij}\) be the retained vector with entries plus one and minus one at the two port layers. Define

\[ \widehat L=\operatorname{diag}(L_0,\ldots,L_0) +\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E(\mathcal G)}b_{ij}b_{ij}^{\mathsf T}, \] \[ V(\bar y)=\frac12\sum_i c_i\bar y_i^{\mathsf T}L_0\bar y_i +\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E(\mathcal G)} [1-\cos(o_j-o_i+\bar y_{j,0}-\bar y_{i,0})]. \]

The first is exactly \(T^{\mathsf T}L_{\rm fine}T\) for the block lift. Internal potentials are tangent quadratics; bridge potentials remain the original nonlinear sine potentials. Equation (2) becomes

\[ \bar x'=-M^{-1}\widehat L\bar x-\gamma M^{-1}\nabla V, \qquad \bar y'=\gamma M^{-1}\widehat L\bar x. \tag{3} \]

Consequently the reduced storage

\[ H_{\rm red}=\tfrac12\bar x^{\mathsf T}\widehat L\bar x+V(\bar y) \]

satisfies, for every retained state and every fixed admitted contact graph,

\[ \boxed{H_{\rm red}'= -(\widehat L\bar x)^{\mathsf T}M^{-1}(\widehat L\bar x)\le0.} \tag{4} \]

The two mixed terms cancel by symmetry of \(M^{-1}\). This is a derived balance of this surrogate, not an assertion that its storage equals the full sine storage away from the reference geometry.

Both \(\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}M\bar x\) and \(\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}M\bar y\) are constant: the gradients and Laplacian have zero total sum. The individual component charges instead obey

\[ (\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}M_i\bar x_i)'=u_{x,i}+\gamma u_{\theta,i}, \qquad (\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}M_i\bar y_i)'=-\gamma u_{x,i}. \tag{5} \]

They cannot be held separately fixed after attachment.

The observed port values are not automatically energy-conjugate outputs. For internal storage alone, put \(a_i=L_0\bar x_i\) and \(b_i=c_iL_0\bar y_i\). Its open-port supply term is

\[ \frac{(a_{i,0}-\gamma b_{i,0})u_{x,i} +\gamma a_{i,0}u_{\theta,i}}{2+d_i}. \]

The internal dissipation is \(-a_i^{\mathsf T}M_i^{-1}a_i\). Summing internal storages alone omits bridge form storage as well as bridge potential. Equation (4) includes both and provides the joined balance; it does not identify \(u_x\bar x_0+u_\theta\bar y_0\) as physical power.

docs.title: A rational control rejects the unchanged one-contact assembly
docs.text:
For the frozen three-component path, set middle port form to one and every other retained form to zero, with all deviations and origins zero. The middle port has four neighbors, so its exact form rate is \(-1\). The adjacent internal layer has rate \(1/2\), and each endpoint component's port has rate \(1/3\). These give actual-degree-weighted charge rate \(-4+2+1+1=0\).

Keeping denominator three at the middle port produces \(-4/3\). Its other rates above remain unchanged, so the actual weighted charge rate becomes \(-16/3+2+1+1=-4/3\). The corresponding phase-charge rate is \(4\gamma/3\), rather than zero. The correct storage loss at this state is \(-17/3\); the erroneous mobility gives \(-7\). Thus nonincreasing storage under some changed metric would not validate the declared model. This exact algebraic control is independent of a numerical trajectory or the reserved formation-family bounds.

docs.title: Uniform error against the full nonlinear fine law
docs.text:
Extend equation (2) to all nine coordinates per component solely as a proof device: linearize internal cycle sine currents about their own twist, retain exact bridge sine currents, and keep the actual fine mobility. Independent reflections fix every central port. This extended surrogate preserves their even subspace, and projection/lift of that subspace gives (2) exactly. The full nonlinear sine law does not generally preserve the same even subspace: quadratic internal terms can generate odd deviations. No such invariance is assumed below.

Write the full ideal comparison as \(x=\gamma v\), \(\theta=\Theta+o+y\), with \(v(0)=y(0)=0\), and put \(\eta=\gamma^2\), \(A=KL\). The diffusion semigroup \(\exp(-At)\) is a maximum-norm contraction, \(\|A\|_\infty\le2\), and the normalized sine field is globally Lipschitz with constant two. Its reference forcing is supported at the central ports. Define

\[ \sigma=\|KS(\Theta+o)\|_\infty =\max_i\frac{|\sum_{j\sim i}\sin(o_j-o_i)|}{2+d_i}. \tag{6} \]

This retains the algebraic sum of incident currents, rather than fitting a forcing from the evaluated response. Suppose

\[ 0\le h<1/3,\qquad C_h=1-\tfrac23\eta h^2>0. \]

Duhamel's formula and \(y'=\eta Av\) give

\[ \|v(t)\|_\infty\le\sigma t+2\int_0^t\|y(s)\|_\infty ds, \qquad \|y(t)\|_\infty\le2\eta\int_0^t\|v(s)\|_\infty ds. \]

For \(B_h=\sup_{0<t\le h}\|v(t)\|_\infty/t\), these imply \(B_h\le\sigma+(2/3)\eta h^2 B_h\). Smoothness at zero and global existence justify the finite supremum. Therefore

\[ \|v(t)\|_\infty\le\frac{\sigma t}{C_h},\qquad \|y(t)\|_\infty\le\frac{\eta\sigma t^2}{C_h} \quad(0\le t\le h). \tag{7} \]

On each internal edge the first-order sine remainder has magnitude at most half the squared deviation gap. Each gap is at most \(2\|y\|_\infty\), and internal degree divided by actual fine degree is at most one. Hence the full normalized internal-field defect is at most \(2\|y\|_\infty^2\), irrespective of the number of components or central contacts. Bridge fields have no reduction defect. In physical form coordinates the complete-row defect is thus at most \(2\gamma^5\sigma^2t^4/C_h^2\).

Both full and extended surrogate fields are globally Lipschitz in the joint maximum norm with constant at most \(2+2\gamma<3\). Variation of constants for the error, or the integral Gronwall inequality, bounds the fine ideal-to-lifted-surrogate discrepancy by

\[ E_{\rm nonlinear}(h) \le\frac{2\gamma^5\sigma^2 h^5}{5C_h^2(1-3h)}. \tag{8} \]

For example, take the supremum of the error on \([0,h]\): its integral inequality is at most the integral of the stated defect plus \(3h\) times that supremum. This proves (8) without evaluating an exponential and covers both form and phase errors, including feedback from generated odd modes. The restriction \(h<1/3\) belongs to this sufficient bound, not to existence of either flow.

Every actual formation-family endpoint has fine maximum-norm distance at most \(\epsilon\) from its ideal comparison state. Global Lipschitz comparison separately bounds its actual full trajectory's distance from the ideal full trajectory by \(\epsilon/(1-3h)\). In particular, arbitrary admitted odd initial errors and their independent component correlations are retained. The whole-window full-state error certificate is

\[ \boxed{E_{\rm full}(h)=\frac{\epsilon}{1-3h} +\frac{2\gamma^5\sigma^2 h^5}{5C_h^2(1-3h)}.} \tag{9} \]

It applies to every fine coordinate after lifting the surrogate and restoring each reference twist and origin. At \(h=0\) it is the initial uncertainty bound. If all origins agree, \(\sigma=0\), so the ideal zero-deviation comparison is stationary; actual preparation errors still remain. The bound is uniform in graph size because of normalized degrees, not because the graph or initial state was omitted.

docs.title: Actual source handoff, support work and joined identity
docs.text:
Reuse the unprobed nonlinear handoff with every original formation source re-admitted. Common phase origins are exact isolated-cycle symmetries. Thus its per-class proof transfers to each component independently without rotating a reached state or modifying any source-family width. The report must establish the actual endpoint bounds before equation (9) becomes a claim about that family.

For the following joined certificate require \(m\ge2\) and connected \(\mathcal G\), and put \(\Delta=\operatorname{diam}(\mathcal G)\). Any fine node lies within four cycle edges of its center, so the joined fine diameter is at most \(\Delta+8\). For \(n=9m\), every mean-zero real vector \(z\) satisfies

\[ \|z\|_2^2\le\frac n4(\max z-\min z)^2 \le\frac{n(\Delta+8)}4z^{\mathsf T}Lz. \]

The first inequality is the bounded-range variance inequality; the second uses a shortest path and Cauchy--Schwarz. Consequently

\[ \lambda_2(L)\ge\lambda_*:=\frac4{9m(\Delta+8)}. \tag{10} \]

This proof also permits cycles in the contact graph. No tree-only stability theorem is being transferred.

The aligned joined target has each component's class twist, a single common phase origin, zero bridge phase gaps, and common form. Internal sine forces cancel and bridge currents vanish, so it is critical for the joined support. In its Euclidean quotient ball of radius \(r\), with \(0<r\le1/12\), every continuous representative of a reference edge gap changes by at most \(\sqrt2r\). The fixed closing-edge integer is retained. Thus all circular gaps remain acute and their cosines are at least

\[ c_r=\cos(4\pi/9+\sqrt2r)>1/20. \]

The acute-chart coercivity argument gives full sine storage excess at least \(\kappa_*\|z\|_2^2\), where

\[ \kappa_*=\tfrac12\lambda_*c_r. \tag{11} \]

Here \(z\) removes the arithmetic common form and phase origins for geometric comparison. Those arithmetic means need not remain constant; the conserved actual-degree-weighted means are retained below.

At contact write \(x_i\) and \(u_i=\theta_i-\Theta_i-o_i\mathbf1\) for the actual component deviations. Their Euclidean norms are at most \(\epsilon\), and their component sums are exactly zero, inherited from the isolated degree-two law. If \(\bar o=m^{-1}\sum_i o_i\), the quotient squared distance obeys

\[ Z_0^2\le 2m\epsilon^2+9\sum_i(o_i-\bar o)^2. \tag{12} \]

The cross terms vanish because the phase residual sum is zero on each component. Replacing the actual correlated family by unrelated absolute boxes would lose this equality.

The cycle Laplacian has largest eigenvalue at most four. Its form and phase storage excesses are each at most \(2\epsilon^2\) per component; the phase gradient at the twist is zero and its Hessian norm is at most four. The added bridge form storage is at most \(d_{\max}\sum_i|x_{i,4}|^2\le d_{\max}m\epsilon^2\). Using \(1-\cos a\le a^2/2\) on each new bridge gives

\[ H_0-H_*\le B_H:=(4+d_{\max})m\epsilon^2 +\frac12\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E} (|o_j-o_i|+2\epsilon)^2. \tag{13} \]

The exact event work is the sum of the added edge storages,

\[ W=\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E}\left\{ \tfrac12(x_{j,4}-x_{i,4})^2+ 1-\cos(o_j-o_i+u_{j,4}-u_{i,4})\right\}, \]

and independently

\[ 0\le W\le B_W:=2|E|\epsilon^2 +\frac12\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E} (|o_j-o_i|+2\epsilon)^2. \tag{14} \]

This supplied work is not a continuous loss reserve. The subsequent full-law balance is exactly

\[ H'=-(Lx)^{\mathsf T}K(Lx)\le0. \]

If \(Z_0^2<r^2\) and \(B_H<\kappa_*r^2\), a first-exit argument traps the actual full family in the acute quotient ball for all future uninterrupted joined flow. All target cycle periods are retained, including the individual C9 windings and the zero periods on the aligned contact cycles. Strict convexity in this chart and the largest invariant zero-loss set give recovery to its unique target geometry on each actual conserved-mean leaf, by the whole-state recovery argument. This identity/recovery conclusion uses the actual full sine storage, not the surrogate balance (4) or its finite error estimate.

Total degree mass is \(M_{\rm tot}=18m+2|E|\). Since each target twist is centered and its central phase is zero, the exact postevent conserved origins are

\[ \mu_x=\frac{\sum_i d_i x_{i,4}}{M_{\rm tot}},\qquad \mu_\theta=\frac{\sum_i(18+d_i)o_i+\sum_i d_i u_{i,4}} {M_{\rm tot}}. \tag{15} \]

Each residual fraction has magnitude at most \(2|E|\epsilon/M_{\rm tot}\). Component origins are not conserved separately after joining. The final common form is \(\mu_x\), and the final common phase origin relative to the aligned twists is \(\mu_\theta\), using the retained continuous lifts.

docs.title: Conservative regional formation and its barriers
docs.text:
Finite winding entry, regional channel balance, distributed source geometry, retention barriers and a robust finite passage under the full conservative environment.

Part of Sine pattern geometry and dissipative capture. Section numbers are stable across the collection; hypotheses and model changes remain local to each result.

docs.title: 35. Conservative exchange can produce finite regional winding
docs.text: Section 27's positive-loss capture theorem does not extend by setting its loss coefficient to zero: its preparation scaling divides by that coefficient. There is instead a direct finite-time mechanism under the conservative complete law. It concerns a receiver's cycle winding, an observation of part of the full network. It does not claim entry into a two-sided invariant full-state trapping set, which remains excluded by the conservative formation boundary.

docs.title: A global full-law phase enclosure
docs.text:
Let the support be finite, connected, simple, undirected and unit-weighted, with at least two nodes. Keep unit held capacities, e=0, w=beta=1, no forcing and no support events. In the declared clock tau=t/pi, the normalized-sine rows are

\[ x'=KS(\theta),\qquad \theta'=KLx,\qquad K=\operatorname{diag}(1/d_i),\quad S_i=\sum_{j\sim i}\sin(\theta_j-\theta_i). \]

Here and below a prime denotes d/dtau. Smooth sine and the linear form row give a unique global solution in real phase lifts; wrapping remains an observation, even through an antipodal crossing. Put v0=KLx(0). Since |S_i|<=d_i and ||KL||_infinity=2, direct integration gives

\[ \boxed{\begin{aligned} \|x(\tau)-x(0)\|_\infty&\le\tau,\\ \|\theta(\tau)-\theta(0)-\tau v_0\|_\infty&\le\tau^2. \end{aligned}} \]

Indeed the phase remainder is the integral of KL(x(s)-x(0)), whose norm is at most 2s. Consequently every oriented edge satisfies the full nonlinear bound

\[ \left|\delta_{ij}(\tau)-\delta_{ij}(0) -\tau(v_{0j}-v_{0i})\right|\le2\tau^2. \]

No linearized trajectory replaces either consumed row. On a supplied interval [a,b] with 0<=a<=b, take the range of the affine edge expression over that interval and add [-2b^2,2b^2]. If each resulting interval lies strictly inside one branch ((2h_ij-1)pi,(2h_ij+1)pi) with declared integer h_ij, the entire solution has those edge offsets throughout the interval. For an oriented cycle, telescoping the actual lifted differences then gives W=-sum(h_ij). A failed enclosure is inconclusive; it does not prove that the actual solution leaves the branch. This is a whole-interval result, not a collection of sampled winding observations.

docs.title: One frozen two-port preparation
docs.text:
Reuse the supplied return-path support: the two cycles (0,1,2,3,4) and (5,6,7,8,9), mediator 10, edges 0-10, 10-5, and the return edge 1-6. This section uses the smooth conservative sine law above; the older native-law equilibrium and pulse certificates on this support are not transferred. Declare

\[ R=\{5,6,7,8,9\},\quad Q=V\setminus R,\qquad x_{10}(0)=24,\quad x_1(0)=-24, \] \[ x_i(0)=0\ (i\notin\{1,10\}),\qquad \theta_i(0)=0\quad\text{for all }i. \]

Thus the receiver starts with uniform form, equal phases and winding zero. Its initial phase velocities are derived from the full nodal law:

\[ (v_{05},v_{06},v_{07},v_{08},v_{09})=(-8,8,0,0,0). \]

The two port degrees remain three. These rates are not independently prescribed receiver inputs: they follow from the retained environmental forms, supplied support and complete KLx row. Freeze the retention interval [1/4,1/3] in tau, equivalently [pi/4,pi/3] in t. Along the oriented receiver cycle the affine gap slopes are (16,-8,0,0,-8). The global enclosure gives, simultaneously throughout that interval,

\[ \begin{aligned} \delta_{56}&\in[34/9,50/9]\subset(\pi,3\pi),\\ \delta_{67},\delta_{95}&\in[-26/9,-16/9]\subset(-\pi,-\pi/2),\\ \delta_{78},\delta_{89}&\in[-2/9,2/9]\subset(-\pi,\pi). \end{aligned} \]

The fixed offsets are therefore (1,0,0,0,0) and the receiver winding is exactly -1 for every time in the frozen interval. Its strict branch margin is at least pi-26/9>0; the other faces are farther away. Since it begins with winding zero, at least one receiver edge crosses an antipodal branch before or at tau=1/4. The smooth dynamics are uninterrupted there. The proof does not locate a unique crossing or certify the receiver's winding at every earlier time.

This is an intentionally limited identity claim. In particular the two outer gaps above are obtuse throughout the interval, so the result is not an acute-sector capture certificate. No attraction, asymptotic winding, indefinite maintenance or complete NFR identity follows.

docs.title: Regional work retains the cross-boundary storage
docs.text:
For any node partition R,Q, define internal storage from edges lying entirely within the region, denoted by E(R):

\[ E_R=\frac12x_R^{\mathsf T}L_Rx_R +\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E(R)}(1-\cos(\theta_j-\theta_i)), \]

and similarly E_Q. Let E_cross sum the same edge storage over the cross-boundary edges exactly once. The actual rates still use full-support q=Lx, S and K, not the isolated regional Laplacians. For i in R put

\[ f_i=\sum_{j\in Q:j\sim i}(x_j-x_i),\qquad s_i=\sum_{j\in Q:j\sim i}\sin(\theta_j-\theta_i). \]

The regional gradients are q_i+f_i and -S_i+s_i. Nodewise cancellation of q_i x_i'-S_i theta_i'=0 under the conservative rows proves

\[ \boxed{E_R'=P_R:=\sum_{i\in R}(f_i x_i'+s_i\theta_i'),\qquad E_Q'=P_Q,\qquad E_{\rm cross}'=-P_R-P_Q.} \]

This is the multi-port specialization of the existing receiver work convention. Both form and phase work are needed. The global storage E=E_R+E_Q+E_cross is conserved; incoming work can later return and is not an irreversible loss term or a reusable event allowance.

For the frozen preparation the initial ledger is exactly

\[ (E_R(0),E_Q(0),E_{\rm cross}(0))=(0,864,576),\qquad E(0)=1440. \]

The environment supplies all nonzero initial form, but the energy stored on its contacts must not be counted again as environmental internal storage. Because both delta_67 and delta_95 lie in (-pi,-pi/2), their phase storage contributions each exceed one. Therefore throughout the retention interval

\[ \boxed{\int_0^\tau P_R(s)\,ds=E_R(\tau)>2.} \]

At the initial instant all sine currents vanish, so x'(0)=0 and P_R(0)=0. The strictly positive integrated work is a conclusion about the subsequent full-network exchange, not an initial power score relabelled as stored energy.

docs.title: Acute winding requires internal phase redistribution
docs.text:
Keep the same law, support and unit capacities, globally equal initial phases, and uniform initial receiver form; environmental form amplitudes may be arbitrary. In a fully acute C5 with winding +1, every principal gap is positive: otherwise the other four, each smaller than pi/2, could not sum to 2pi. The negative-winding case has the reversed signs. The sum of the two inner gaps 7->8->9 therefore has magnitude strictly between pi/2 and pi, because the other three contribute less than 3pi/2. In particular

\[ \boxed{\cos(\theta_9-\theta_7)<0} \]

is necessary for fully acute winding at any time. This is a correlation of existing phases, not a new coordinate or an additional law. The relevant organization is an oriented phase pattern, not equality of all phases.

The shared inner path yields a stronger time restriction than treating its edges as independent. Write z=theta_9-theta_7. The full rows give

\[ z'=x_9-x_7+\frac{x_6-x_5}{2},\qquad z(0)=z'(0)=0, \] \[ |z''|\le3,\qquad |z(\tau)|\le\frac32\tau^2. \]

The derivative bound follows from |x_i'|<=1. Equivalently the exact pair-current coefficients in z''=c^T S are c_9=1/2,c_7=-1/2,c_6=1/6,c_5=-1/6, with all others zero; sum_edges |c_i-c_j|=3. This retains the telescoping correlation instead of adding two independent edge-error radii.

If tau^2<=pi/3, the individual inner raw gaps have magnitude at most 2tau^2<=2pi/3<pi by the global enclosure, so their principal sum is exactly z. Acute winding would require |z|>pi/2, contradicting the bound. Thus tau^2>pi/3 is necessary, independently of environmental amplitude. The existing [1/4,1/3] winding interval lies entirely inside this exclusion. The inequality is not an optimal entry time or an obstruction after its cutoff. Additional ports, nonuniform receiver form, nonflat preparation or different capacities require their own calculation.

docs.title: The complete rows already transmit phase motion to the inner path
docs.text:
There is an explicit local propagation mechanism, although it does not prove finite acute entry. Put A=KL. At globally flat phase, x'(0)=0 and theta''(0)=0, while differentiation of the same complete sine rows gives

\[ v_0=Ax(0),\qquad x''(0)=-A^2x(0),\qquad \boxed{\theta'''(0)=-A^3x(0).} \]

For the supplied preparation x_10=H,x_1=-H, all other forms zero, the inner phase third derivatives at nodes (7,8,9) are (5H/9,0,-5H/9). For example, the receiver form second derivatives are (7H/9,-7H/9,H/6,0,-H/6). Hence

\[ z'''(0)=-10H/9,\qquad z(\tau)=-5H\tau^3/27+O(\tau^5). \]

The odd phase powers follow from the exact time-reversal symmetry about this flat-phase preparation: after removing its common phase origin, theta(-tau)=-theta(tau) and x(-tau)=x(tau). At H=24, the leading inner spread is -40tau^3/9, in the same orientation as the certified negative winding. This local expansion has no supplied finite-time remainder; extrapolating it past the necessary-time cutoff would not certify entry. analyze_sine_conservative_phase_transport retains the admitted source, full-row derivatives and correlated transport bounds without replacing the nonlinear law by its Taylor polynomial.

docs.title: A finite regional work budget can retain an admitted acute state
docs.text:
There is a sufficient continuation condition that retains form as well as phase. On an acute winding-one C5, convexity of 1-cos(delta) gives the minimum phase storage

\[ V_5=5\bigl(1-\cos(2\pi/5)\bigr). \]

At an acute-sector boundary at least one gap is pi/2. The other four sum to 3pi/2; convexity minimizes their storage at 3pi/8 each. A -pi/2 boundary gap cannot carry winding one with the remaining four gaps in [-pi/2,pi/2]. Reflection gives the negative-winding case. Thus the exact minimum phase storage on either sector's boundary is

\[ \boxed{B=1+4\bigl(1-\cos(3\pi/8)\bigr) =5-4\cos(3\pi/8).} \]

Suppose an independently admitted full state at time T has acute receiver winding +1 or -1. For a declared finite horizon h, suppose a proved bound on its actual boundary work satisfies

\[ E_R(T)+\sup_{0\le s\le h}\int_T^{T+s}P_R(u)\,du \le E_{\max}<B. \]

The exact regional balance then prevents a first acute-face exit before T+h: at such an exit phase storage alone would be at least B. Throughout this interval the internal form storage also satisfies F_R<=E_max-V_5<B-V_5, where B-V_5 is approximately 0.01435 in the declared units. A strict budget supplies a positive acute margin and retains the full regional form differences; it is not just a winding sample. The actual full-support phase rates and environmental work remain part of the state and balance. This uses the phase-barrier geometry of the sector theorem, not its positive-loss capture conclusion. It supplies no entry from a flat receiver by itself.

For the frozen H=24 preparation, entry into this low-storage region would require genuine return of storage to the environment. At tau=1/4, the existing phase bound gives

\[ \delta_{56}\in[31/8,33/8]\subset(\pi,4\pi/3),\qquad \delta_{67},\delta_{95}\in[-17/8,-15/8]. \]

The first edge has phase storage greater than 3/2. Each outer edge has storage greater than 5/4, since 15/8>7pi/12 and cos(7pi/12)<-1/4. Consequently E_R(1/4)>4. Since B<7/2, any later entry time T with E_R(T)<B must satisfy

\[ \boxed{\int_{1/4}^{T}P_R(u)\,du =E_R(T)-E_R(1/4)<-1/2.} \]

This necessary net return is compatible with global conservation and is not dissipation. It identifies internal redistribution and export, beyond the already proved incoming transfer, as obligations of a low-storage entry claim. It does not exclude an acute high-energy passage and does not prove that the required return or entry occurs. No new trajectory is inferred from these analytic restrictions.

docs.title: A bounded full-state organization control
docs.text:
The prospective declaration retains the same support and conservative complete law, with H=3, all initial phases zero and unit capacities. Receiver initial phase velocities are (-1,+1,0,0,0) in tau; total initial storage is 45/2, partitioned as receiver 0, environment 27/2 and cross-boundary 9. This normalizes one preparation for study. It is not an optimal amplitude or a selected law.

The horizon is t in [0,12], using original structural time, with 256 fixed steps of 3/64 and Taylor order 10. The target is a contiguous whole-time acute receiver winding interval of at least 1/4 in t, with fixed edge branches and acute margin at least 1/16 radian, certified by a strict lower bound greater than that threshold. These numerical and observation choices are supplied policies. Full regional form, phase rates, storage and signed boundary work remain observable; the target does not require the stronger low-storage protection condition above.

The producer freezes the protocol, source archive and runtime before invoking the shared Picard/Taylor forecast. The regional observer distinguishes certified finite retention, exclusion on a fully covered horizon and unresolved or partial evidence. No amplitude, horizon or solver budget is adjusted in response to the reserved evolution. A numerical enclosure failure cannot become a mathematical impossibility result.

The frozen response certifies all 256 whole-time tubes, covering the entire declared horizon. Its outcome is acute_winding_excluded_on_horizon, with no evaluation error or unresolved numerical step. Every receiver edge remains acute and all principal-branch offsets remain zero, so receiver winding is exactly zero throughout. The minimum certified acute margin exceeds 0.348 radian. Each tube also independently excludes acute unit winding through a nonnegative two-hop phase cosine. These are full-interval exclusions, not an inference from endpoint sampling.

The exchange nevertheless changes the receiver. Its endpoint internal storage is approximately 5.19076, consisting of form storage 4.17198 and phase storage 1.01878. Every tube bounds phase storage below 1.263, whereas acute unit winding on this C5 requires at least V_5=5*(1-cos(2*pi/5)), approximately 3.45492. The signed regional power is strictly positive on 224 tubes and strictly negative on 23; its interval contains zero on the remaining 9. Thus incoming and returned work both occur, but total storage exceeding V_5 does not supply the required phase geometry. The endpoint's nonzero relative phase rates also preclude interpreting it as phase locking or equilibrium. The exact interval record, not these rounded display values, owns the evidence.

This closes the declared H=3 control negatively without retuning preparation, horizon or target. It does not exclude later winding, other preparations or other definitions of an organized pattern. In particular, nonuniform form and locally acute phases can be organized without nonzero winding; winding is the selected identity discriminator here, not a universal NFR definition. This response does not establish how boundary exchange and reversible internal form/phase conversion supply directed phase organization. The total-work ledger alone cannot decide it. The separate same-orbit construction proves a conditional existence result with a different preparation and support; the failed response here remains retained without replay.

docs.text:
Resetting the two nonzero environmental forms to zero, while retaining the same support, law, receiver state and phases, gives an exact stationary control. This is a preparation control, not an equal-energy comparison. A distinct support control removes 1-6 before initialization and keeps the supplied forms. Then the receiver reflection (6 9)(7 8) fixes the entire preparation and law. By the existing single-port symmetry obstruction, receiver winding stays zero whenever no receiver edge is antipodal. comparison.regional_storage_balance(region=...) in the shared sine owner also supports the existing general sine coefficients and nonnegative capacities. In its original structural clock t, the same calculation gives dE_R/dt=-e*sum_R(nu_i/d_i)*q_i^2+P_R, where phase storage and phase boundary work carry the declared beta. The complement has its own full-node loss; the cross-edge derivative remains -P_R-P_Q. This snapshot identity does not integrate boundary work or substitute for the finite-window theorem. No inverse capacity is needed at zero capacity.

The analytic declaration precedes the retained certificate and controls. The producer reuses the write-once evidence transport and retains its source archive. There is no reserved trajectory: the global inequality certifies every time in the declared window. Independent tests check the complete nodal jet, telescoping, storage partitions and both controls without fitting a response.

The analytic winding theorem establishes one conditional mechanism for acquiring and retaining a regional winding through conservative environmental exchange. The large, asymmetric environmental preparation and both ports are supplied premises. Their origin, a mechanism selecting this preparation, a low-budget formation law and physical identification remain open. docs.title: 36. Regional channel balance and phase accessibility
Separate internal conversion from boundary input
docs.text:
Retain the complete smooth sine law on fixed simple connected unit support, held nonnegative capacities and no forcing or events. Set K=diag(nu_i/d_i) using full-network degrees, a=w/pi and storage scale beta>0. For a region R, let q_R=L_R*x_R and S_R be its internal form gradient and internal sine current. External contributions are

\[ f_i=\sum_{j\notin R,\,j\sim i}(x_j-x_i),\qquad s_i=\sum_{j\notin R,\,j\sim i}\sin(\theta_j-\theta_i). \]

Thus the restriction of the full form gradient is q_R-f, and the full sine current is S_R+s. The actual regional rows in original structural time are

\[ \dot x_R=K_R[-e(q_R-f)+a(S_R+s)],\qquad \dot\theta_R=\frac a\beta K_R(q_R-f). \]

Write internal storage as E_R=F_R+beta*V_R, with F_R=x_R^T L_R x_R/2 and V_R=sum_internal(1-cos(delta)). Its gradients are q_R and -S_R. Define

\[ J_R=a q_R^\mathsf T K_R S_R,\quad B_F=a q_R^\mathsf T K_R s,\quad B_V=a S_R^\mathsf T K_R f,\quad D_F=e q_R^\mathsf T K_R(q_R-f). \]

Direct differentiation yields the exact identities

\[ \boxed{\dot F_R=J_R+B_F-D_F,\qquad \frac{d(\beta V_R)}{dt}=-J_R+B_V.} \]

Positive J_R converts phase storage into form storage, while its negative converts form into phase. B_F is the input to internal form storage from external phase currents; B_V is the input to internal phase storage from external form contrasts. They can have either sign. D_F is signed and is not the nonnegative full-node loss in the existing regional ledger.

Indeed that ledger has P_R=f^T*xdot_R+beta*s^T*thetadot_R and D_R=e*(q_R-f)^T K_R(q_R-f). Expanding both gives P_R-D_R=B_F+B_V-D_F. The cross term f^T K_R s cancels, while internal conversion cancels between the two storage rows. The old form and phase conjugate boundary-work fields are therefore not the new inputs to the individual stores and must not be renamed as such. These identities remain valid at zero capacity and require no inverse capacity.

For e=0, the cumulative phase-directed work satisfies

\[ \beta[V_R(t)-V_R(0)]=\int_0^t[-J_R(u)+B_V(u)]\,du. \]

This is a derived balance under the declared complete law, not an extra pressure, damping term or controller. Instantaneous rates and their running integrals are different observations. Retained environmental state supplies both boundary inputs; eliminating it requires the separate memory contract.

docs.title: Equal storage does not determine the initial phase response
docs.text:
If all receiver phases are initially equal, the internal phase gradient vanishes. The second derivative of its weighted phase storage is then

\[ \boxed{\frac{d^2(\beta V_R)}{dt^2}(0) =\beta\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E_R} [\dot\theta_j(0)-\dot\theta_i(0)]^2.} \]

The terms involving phase acceleration vanish because every internal sine is zero. The rates on the right are those of the full support, including external form contrasts and full degrees. A common initial phase rotation does not grow phase storage. Relative velocities, rather than total storage alone, determine this initial curvature. This is a local-in-time identity; it cannot certify later branch passage or retention.

An exact control reuses the two-C5/intermediary support and return edge 1-6. Take e=0,w=beta=1, unit capacity, all phases zero and all forms zero except x_10=H and x_1=+H or -H. Both preparations have exactly the same storage partitions: receiver 0, complement 3H^2/2, cross-boundary H^2. In tau=t/pi, receiver phase rates and initial phase-storage curvature are

Environmental form Receiver phase rates in cycle order d^2 V_R/dtau^2(0) x_10=H, x_1=-H (-H/3,+H/3,0,0,0) 2H^2/3 x_10=H, x_1=+H (-H/3,-H/3,0,0,0) 2H^2/9

For H!=0, orientation changes initial phase growth by a factor of three at identical storage, including each regional partition. Original-time curvature divides these entries by pi^2. The raw conserved form means differ and are retained; if a common mean leaf is required, independent uniform form shifts set them equal without changing either field or any storage. No response is simulated, and neither preparation is thereby proved to form an acute twist.

docs.title: A running phase barrier for any acute unit-winding entry
docs.text:
The pure-phase C5 minimax is 7/2: every continuous phase path from consensus to a uniform unit twist reaches V_R>=7/2. This is a geometric result on the phase torus, independent of the positive-loss assumptions of other results using it.

It also applies when the endpoint is any fully acute state of winding +1 or -1. At that endpoint keep its integer edge offsets and linearly interpolate its principal gaps to the uniform gaps +2*pi/5 or -2*pi/5. Their sum remains +2*pi or -2*pi, so the change lifts to a continuous nodal phase path. All gaps remain in (-pi/2,pi/2); convexity of 1-cos there bounds this appended path's storage by its initial endpoint storage. If the original path never reached 7/2, the concatenation would contradict the minimax. This establishes a necessary running, not final, condition:

\[ \boxed{\text{flat receiver reaches an acute unit-winding state by }T \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \max_{0\le t\le T}\int_0^t[-J_R(u)+B_V(u)]\,du \ge \frac72\beta.} \]

Exceeding this bound does not supply oriented passage or a particular target; the two signs of winding have identical storage. Remaining below it excludes acute entry, not arbitrary nonacute winding. Nor does the barrier exclude an already prepared acute state. The zero initial potential in this formula uses flat phase; the larger sector argument retains the initial potential and gives a broader exclusion without it. A signed branch crossing still depends on the actual relative phase velocity, and protected retention still requires its own full-state and work bounds.

docs.title: Shared implementation and evidence boundary
docs.text: regional_storage_balance in the comparison owner exposes these channels for both region and complement, preserving the original conjugate work ledger. The same kernel consumes admitted whole-time boxes in assess_sine_regional_channels. It integrates interval rates over each complete step, retains endpoint balance residuals and distinguishes complete horizons from validated prefixes. The 7/2 exclusion is conditional on certified flat initial receiver phase and applies only to the validated prefix. Taylor endpoint enclosures remain numerical premises; neither export nor re-reading authenticates their origin. The API contract owns admission and projection details. These observers add no evolution law.
